sentences.zh: 万俟普子洛可硃渾元劉豐破六韓常金祚劉貴蔡俊韓賢尉長命王懷任祥子胄莫多婁貸文子敬顯厙狄回洛厙狄盛張保洛賀拔仁曲珍段琛尉摽摽子相貴康得韓建業封輔相范舍樂牒舍樂侯莫陳相薛孤延斛律羌舉子孝卿張瓊宋顯王則慕容紹宗叱列平步大汗薩薛修義慕容儼厙狄伏連潘樂彭樂暴顯皮景和綦連猛元景安獨孤永業鮮于世榮傅伏

sentences.zh: 万俟普

translations.literal: Wan Sipu
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sipu

sentences.zh: 万俟洛

translations.literal: Wan Si Luo
translations.idiomatic: Wan Si Luo

sentences.zh: 洛，字受洛幹，隨孝武入關，除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Luo, styled Shouluogan, followed Emperor Xiaowu into the Pass and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, whose style was Shouluogan, followed Emperor Xiaowu through the Pass and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天平中，隨父東歸，封建昌郡公，再遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: During the Tianping era he followed his father eastward, was enfeoffed as Duke of Changchang commandery, and was promoted again to Commandant of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he followed his father eastward, was made Duke of Changchang, and was promoted again to Commandant of the Army.

sentences.zh: 初，神武以其父普尊老，特崇禮之，嘗親扶上馬。

translations.literal: At first, because Gao Huan regarded Luo's father Pu as an honored elder, he treated him with special courtesy and once personally helped him mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gao Huan, honoring Luo's father Pu as an elder, treated him with exceptional courtesy and once helped him mount his horse in person.

sentences.zh: 洛免冠稽首，願出萬死力以報深恩。

translations.literal: Luo removed his cap and prostrated himself, vowing to exert strength unto ten thousand deaths to repay this profound favor.
translations.idiomatic: Luo doffed his cap and kowtowed, pledging to give his utmost—even unto death ten thousand times over—to repay so deep a kindness.

sentences.zh: 及河陰之戰，諸軍北度橋，洛以一軍不動，謂西人曰：「万俟受洛幹在此，能來可來也！」

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin, when the armies crossed the bridge northward, Luo held one army unmoving and said to the Western forces: "Wanqi Shouluogan is here—if you can come, then come!"
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin, as the armies crossed the bridge to the north, Luo held one division steady and called to the Western army: "Wanqi Shouluogan is here—come if you dare!

sentences.zh: 西人畏而去之。

translations.literal: The Western forces feared him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Western forces feared him and drew off.

sentences.zh: 神武名其所營地為回洛。

translations.literal: Gao Huan named the place where he had camped Huiluo (Return of Luo).
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan named the place where Luo had camped Huiluo—"Luo's Return."

sentences.zh: 洛慷慨有氣節，勇銳冠世。

translations.literal: Luo was magnanimous and possessed moral resolve; his courage and keenness were unmatched in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was open-handed and principled, and his valor and dash were unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師、大司馬、太尉、錄尚書，諡曰武。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Masters of Writing; his posthumous title was Martial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Martial.

sentences.zh: 可硃渾元

translations.literal: Kezhui Hunyuan
translations.idiomatic: Kezhui Hunyuan

sentences.zh: 可硃渾元，字道元，自雲遼東人也。

translations.literal: Kezhui Hunyuan, styled Daoyuan, claimed to be a man of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhui Hunyuan, styled Daoyuan, said of himself that he was from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖護野肱，為懷朔鎮將，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Huyegong was general of Huaiyuan Garrison, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Huyegong served as general of Huaiyuan Garrison, and the clan made its home there.

sentences.zh: 元寬仁有武略，少與神武相知。

translations.literal: Hunyuan was generous and humane and possessed military stratagems; in youth he became acquainted with Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Hunyuan was broad-minded and humane, skilled in military affairs, and in his youth he came to know Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮以為別將，隸爾硃天光。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong appointed him a separate commander subordinate to Erzhu Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong made him a separate commander under Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 平万俟醜奴等，以功封東縣伯。

translations.literal: He pacified Moqi Chounu and others, and for his achievements was enfeoffed Baron of Dongxian.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified Moqi Chounu and others and, for his merit, was enfeoffed as Baron of Dongxian.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝立，累遷渭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was established, he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Hunyuan rose through repeated promotions to Governor of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元既早為神弄知遇，兼其母兄在東，恆表疏與神武往來。

translations.literal: Hunyuan had long been favored by Gao Huan, and since his mother and elder brother were in the east, he constantly exchanged memorials with Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Hunyuan had long enjoyed Gao Huan's favor, and with his mother and elder brother still in the east, he kept up a steady exchange of memorials with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 周文帝有疑心，元乃率所部三千戶，發渭州，西北度烏蘭津，曆河、源二州境，乃得東出。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou was suspicious; Hunyuan thereupon led his following of three thousand households, set out from Wei Prefecture, crossed Wulan Ford northwestward, passed through the territories of He and Yuan provinces, and thus was able to go out east.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen of Zhou grew suspicious, Hunyuan led his three thousand households out of Wei Prefecture, crossed Wulan Ford to the northwest, traversed He and Yuan provinces, and at last broke out to the east.

sentences.zh: 靈州刺史曹掞待元甚厚。

translations.literal: Cao Yan, Governor of Ling Prefecture, treated Hunyuan very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yan, governor of Ling Prefecture, received Hunyuan with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 掞女婿劉豐生與元深相結，遂資遣元。

translations.literal: Yan's son-in-law Liu Fengsheng was deeply united with Hunyuan, and they furnished supplies and sent Hunyuan on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son-in-law Liu Fengsheng was bound to Hunyuan in close alliance, and together they supplied him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 元從靈州東北入雲州界。

translations.literal: Hunyuan entered Yunzhou territory from the northeast of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hunyuan entered Yunzhou from the northeast of Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周文每遣兵邀元，元戰必摧之。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhou Wen dispatched troops to intercept Hunyuan, Hunyuan fought and invariably shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Zhou Wen sent troops to cut him off, Hunyuan met them in battle and always broke them.

sentences.zh: 神武聞其來，遣平陽太守高崇持金環一枚賜元，並運資糧候接。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan heard he was coming, he sent Pingyang Administrator Gao Chong bearing a gold ring to bestow on Hunyuan, and also transported provisions to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of his approach, Gao Huan sent Pingyang Administrator Gao Chong with a gold ring as a gift and had provisions moved up to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 元至，引見執手。

translations.literal: When Hunyuan arrived, Gao Huan received him in audience and took his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunyuan arrived, Gao Huan received him in audience and clasped his hand.

sentences.zh: 後進并州刺史，以貪污劾，特見原。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Governor of Bing Province; he was impeached for corruption but was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to governor of Bing Province; though impeached for corruption, he was specially forgiven.

sentences.zh: 累以軍功拜司空。

translations.literal: Through repeated military achievements he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On accumulated military merit he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封扶風郡王，位太傅、太師。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao period he was enfeoffed Prince of Fufeng commandery and held the posts of Grand Tutor and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign he was made Prince of Fufeng and held the posts of Grand Tutor and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈假黃鉞、太宰、太師。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, Grand Steward, and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow battle-axe, the title Grand Steward, and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 元用兵務持重，未嘗敗。

translations.literal: In employing troops Hunyuan always stressed steadiness and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In command Hunyuan always favored steadiness and was never defeated.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享文襄廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huangjian era he was granted co-worship in the temple court of Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huangjian era he was given a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Wenxiang's temple.

sentences.zh: 子長舉襲。

translations.literal: His son Changju inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changju succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 可硃天元

translations.literal: Kezhui Tianyuan
translations.idiomatic: Kezhui Tianyuan

sentences.zh: 道元弟天元，亦有將略，便弓馬，封昌陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's younger brother Tianyuan also possessed military stratagems, was skilled with bow and horse, and was enfeoffed Baron of Changyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan's younger brother Tianyuan was likewise skilled in generalship and adept with bow and horse; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changyang.

sentences.zh: 天保初，位殿中、七兵二尚書。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao period he held the posts of Director of the Palace and the two Ministers of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he served as Director of the Palace and as Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都督、滄州刺史，諡曰恭武。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously awarded Area Commander and Governor of Cang Prefecture; his posthumous title was Reverent Martial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made area commander and governor of Cang Prefecture, with the posthumous name Reverent Martial.

sentences.zh: 可硃天和

translations.literal: Kezhui Tianhe
translations.idiomatic: Kezhui Tianhe

sentences.zh: 天元弟天和，以道元勳重，尚東平長公主，賜爵宜安鄉男。

translations.literal: Tianyuan's younger brother Tianhe, because Daoyuan's merit was weighty, married the Eldest Princess of Dongping and was granted the title Baronet of Yi'an township.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyuan's younger brother Tianhe, on account of Daoyuan's great merit, married the Eldest Princess of Dongping and was granted the rank of Baronet of Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，加駙馬都尉，位開府儀同三司，封成皋郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication, Tianhe was additionally made Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law, held the office of Grand Master with golden seal and triple staff of equal precedence with the Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed Duke of Chenggao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan took the throne, Tianhe was further made Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law, appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal with triple staff, and enfeoffed as Duke of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 濟南即位，加特進，改封博陵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jinan took the throne, he was additionally made Special Advance and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Boling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jinan succeeded, Tianhe was made Special Advance and his title was changed to Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 與楊愔同被殺。

translations.literal: He was executed together with Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He was put to death together with Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 劉豐，字豐生，普樂人也。

translations.literal: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, was a man of Pule.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, was from Pule.

sentences.zh: 有雄姿壯氣，果毅絕人。

translations.literal: He had a heroic bearing and stalwart spirit; his resolution and daring were unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: He had a heroic bearing and commanding presence, and his resolution and daring were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 破六韓拔陵之亂，以守城功，除普樂太守，山鹿縣公，靈州鎮城大都督。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Poli Han Baling, for his achievement in defending the city he was appointed Administrator of Pule, Duke of Shanlu county, and Great Area Commander of the garrison city of Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the rebellion of Poli Han Baling, for defending the city he was made administrator of Pule, Duke of Shanlu, and great area commander of Ling Prefecture's garrison city.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳與靈州刺史曹掞不睦，豐助掞守。

translations.literal: Heba Yue was on bad terms with Cao Yan, Governor of Ling Prefecture; Feng assisted Yan in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue was at odds with Cao Yan, governor of Ling Prefecture, and Feng helped Yan hold the city.

sentences.zh: 嶽將自討掞，為侯莫陳悅所殺。

translations.literal: Yue was about to campaign against Yan himself when he was killed by Houmo Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was on the point of marching against Yan in person when he was killed by Houmo Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 周文帝遣行台趙善、大都督万俟受洛幹復來攻圍，引河灌之，掞與豐堅守不下。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou sent Mobile Headquarters Commander Zhao Shan and Great Area Commander Wanqi Shouluogan to attack and besiege again; they diverted the river to flood the city, but Yan and Feng held firm and the city did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou sent Zhao Shan of the mobile headquarters and the great area commander Wanqi Shouluogan to besiege the city again; they diverted the river to flood it, yet Yan and Feng held out and the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 豐乃東奔神武，神武以豐為南汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Feng then fled east to Gao Huan, who appointed him Governor of Southern Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng then fled east to Gao Huan, who made him governor of Southern Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，豐功居先，神武執其手嗟賞之。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin, Feng's merit ranked first; Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin Feng's merit stood first; Gao Huan took his hand and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 及王思政據長社，豐與高嶽等攻之。

translations.literal: When Wang Sizheng held Changshe, Feng joined Gao Yue and others in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng held Changshe, Feng joined Gao Yue and others in the siege.

sentences.zh: 先是訛言大魚道上行，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a rumor that a great fish would travel along the road, and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread that a great fish would pass along the road, and the people were sorely troubled by it.

sentences.zh: 豐建水攻策，遏洧水灌城。

translations.literal: Feng devised a strategy of water attack, damming the Wei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Feng proposed a water assault, damming the Wei River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 水長，魚鱉皆遊焉。

translations.literal: As the water rose, fish and turtles all swam there.
translations.idiomatic: As the waters rose, fish and turtles swam through the streets.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，豐與行台慕容紹宗見忽有暴風從東北來，正晝昏暗，飛沙走礫，船纜忽絕，漂至城下。

translations.literal: When the city was about to fall, Feng and Mobile Headquarters Commander Murong Shaozong suddenly saw a violent wind come from the northeast; at high noon it grew dark, sand and stones flew, the boat cables suddenly snapped, and the boats drifted to beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the city was about to fall, Feng and Murong Shaozong of the mobile headquarters saw a sudden gale rise from the northeast; at midday the sky went dark, sand and stones flew, the mooring lines snapped, and the boats drifted under the walls.

sentences.zh: 豐拍浮向土山，為浪激，不時至。

translations.literal: Feng beat the water and floated toward an earthen hill, but the waves struck him and he did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Feng struck the water and swam toward an earthen mound, but the waves drove him and he could not reach it in time.

sentences.zh: 西人鉤之，並為敵所害。

translations.literal: The Westerners hooked them with grappling irons, and both were killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners snagged them with hooks, and both were slain by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 豐壯勇善戰，死日，朝野駭惋。

translations.literal: Feng was stalwart, brave, and skilled in battle; on the day of his death court and commonalty were struck with shock and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was powerful, brave, and skilled in war; at his death court and country were shaken with dismay.

sentences.zh: 贈大司馬、司徒公、尚書令，諡武忠。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Marshal, Duke of the Masters of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title Martial and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Marshal, Duke of the Masters of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Martial and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子曄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ye inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 第三子龍，有巧思，位亦通顯。

translations.literal: The third son Long had ingenious talent and also attained prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Long was ingenious in design and likewise rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，曆將作大匠，卒于領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Master of Works and died in the post of General-in-Chief of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Kaihuang reign he served as Master of Works and died while holding the post of General-in-Chief of the Army.

sentences.zh: 八子俱非嫡妻所生。

translations.literal: All eight sons were born not of the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: All eight sons were born to women other than the principal wife.

sentences.zh: 每一子所生喪，諸子皆為制服三年。

translations.literal: Whenever any one son's birth mother died, all the sons donned mourning garments for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever any one son's mother died, all the brothers wore mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 武平中，痈所生喪，諸弟並請解官，朝廷義而不許。

translations.literal: During the Wuping era, when Yong's birth mother died, all the younger brothers requested to resign office; the court, honoring their righteousness, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuping, when Yong's mother died, all the younger brothers asked to leave office; the court, moved by their filial intent, would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 破六韓常

translations.literal: Poli Hanchang
translations.idiomatic: Poli Hanchang

sentences.zh: 破六韓常，單于之裔也。

translations.literal: Poli Hanchang was a descendant of the Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Poli Hanchang was descended from the Xiongnu shanyu.

sentences.zh: 初呼廚貌入朝漢，為魏武所留，遣其叔父右賢王去卑監本國戶。

translations.literal: At first Huchuqian came to court the Han; he was detained by Emperor Wu of Wei, who sent his uncle the Right Worthy King Qubei to oversee the households of their native state.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Huchuqian came to pay court to the Han; Emperor Wu of Wei detained him and sent his uncle, the Right Worthy King Qubei, to oversee the people of their homeland.

sentences.zh: 魏氏方興，率部南轉，去卑遣弟右谷蠡王潘六奚率軍北禦。

translations.literal: As the Wei dynasty was rising, he led his tribes southward in migration; Qubei sent his younger brother the Right Guli King Panliuxi to lead an army north to resist.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei house was on the rise, the tribes moved south; Qubei sent his younger brother, the Right Guli King Panliuxi, north with an army to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，奚及五子俱沒于魏，其子孫遂以潘六奚為氏。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; Xi and his five sons were all taken by Wei, and their descendants thereupon took Panliuxi as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated; Xi and his five sons all fell into Wei's hands, and their descendants took Panliuxi as their surname.

sentences.zh: 後人訛誤，以為破六韓。

translations.literal: Later men erred in transmission and took it to be Poli Han.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations misread the name and wrote it as Poli Han.

sentences.zh: 世領部落。

translations.literal: For generations they led the tribal confederation.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they led the tribe.

sentences.zh: 父孔雀，少驍勇，背其宗人拔陵，率部降爾硃榮。

translations.literal: His father Kongque was brave and daring in youth; he turned against his clansman Baling, led his tribes to surrender to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kongque was bold and valiant in youth; he broke with his kinsman Baling and led his people to submit to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 詔封永安縣侯，第一領人酋長。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him Marquis of Yong'an county and Chief of the First Leading Peoples.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was made Marquis of Yong'an and chief of the first leading peoples.

sentences.zh: 常，孔雀少子，沉敏有膽略，善騎射。

translations.literal: Chang, Kongque's youngest son, was deep and keen, possessed courage and stratagem, and was skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, Kongque's youngest son, was thoughtful and quick-witted, bold in counsel, and expert in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，常居河西。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Chang resided west of the River.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Chang remained west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 天平中，與冀州刺史万俟受洛幹等東歸，神武上為武衛將軍。

translations.literal: During Tianping he returned east together with Wanqi Shouluogan, Governor of Ji Prefecture, and others; Gao Huan memorialized to appoint him General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he returned east with Wanqi Shouluogan, governor of Ji Prefecture, and others; Gao Huan had him appointed General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，封廣川縣公，拜太子太保。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed Duke of Guangchuan county and appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne he was made Duke of Guangchuan and appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒于滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while Governor of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as governor of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令、司徒公、太傅、第一領人酋長、假王，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Masters of Works, Grand Tutor, Chief of the First Leading Peoples, and Acting King; posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Masters of Works, Grand Tutor, chief of the first leading peoples, and acting king, with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 金祚，字神敬，安定人也。

translations.literal: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zuo, styled Shenjing, was from Anding.

sentences.zh: 性驍雄，尚氣俠。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and heroic and valued spirited chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fierce and bold, and he prized honor and daring.

sentences.zh: 魏末，以軍功至太中大夫，隨元天穆討平邢杲。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, through military achievements he rose to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and followed Yuan Tianmu in campaigning to pacify Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei, on military merit he rose to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and followed Yuan Tianmu in putting down Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 曆涇、岐二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Jing and Qi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Jing and Qi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後大行台賀拔嶽表授東雍州刺史，令討仇池氏楊紹先於百頃。

translations.literal: Later the Great Mobile Headquarters Commander Heba Yue memorialized to appoint him Governor of Eastern Yong Prefecture and ordered him to campaign against Yang Shaoqian of the Chouchi clan at Baiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Heba Yue of the great mobile headquarters had him appointed governor of Eastern Yong and sent him to attack Yang Shaoqian of Chouchi at Baiqing.

sentences.zh: 未還，岳為侯莫陳悅所殺。

translations.literal: Before he returned, Yue was killed by Houmo Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could return, Yue was killed by Houmo Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 祚克仇池還，莫知所歸。

translations.literal: Zuo took Chouchi and returned, but did not know to whom he should submit.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Chouchi and returning, Zuo did not know which side to join.

sentences.zh: 俄而神武遣行台侯景慰諭，祚遂解甲而還，封安定縣公。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Gao Huan sent Mobile Headquarters Commander Hou Jing to comfort and instruct him; Zuo thereupon laid down his arms and returned, and was enfeoffed Duke of Anding county.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan sent Hou Jing of the mobile headquarters to reassure him; Zuo laid down his arms and came over, and was made Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 後隨魏孝武西入，周文帝以祚為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward; Duke Wen of Zhou appointed Zuo Governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu west; Duke Wen of Zhou made him governor of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曆太僕、衛尉二卿。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of the Imperial Stud and Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He held office in turn as Minister of the Imperial Stud and Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 尋除東北道大都督、晉州刺史，入據東雍州。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Great Area Commander of the Northeast Route and Governor of Jin Prefecture, and entered to hold Eastern Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made great area commander of the northeast route and governor of Jin Prefecture, and took possession of Eastern Yong.

sentences.zh: 神武遣尉景攻降之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sent Wei Jing to attack and compel his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Wei Jing to attack him until he submitted.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，以大都督從破西軍，除華州刺史。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Mangshan, as Great Area Commander he followed in the defeat of the Western army and was appointed Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Mangshan, as great area commander he took part in defeating the Western army and was appointed governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 文宣受禪，加開府儀同三司，別封臨濟縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication, he was additionally granted the office of Grand Master with golden seal and triple staff of equal precedence with the Three Excellencies, and was separately enfeoffed Viscount of Linji county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan took the throne, Zuo was further made Grand Master of the Golden Seal with triple staff and separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Linji.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was posthumously awarded Duke of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Duke of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 劉貴，秀容陽曲人也。

translations.literal: Liu Gui was a native of Yangqu in Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui was from Yangqu in Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 剛格有氣斷。

translations.literal: He was stern in character and possessed a resolute spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and resolute by nature, he had a forceful spirit.

sentences.zh: 曆爾硃榮府騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as Cavalry Commandant in Erzhu Rong's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as cavalry commandant on Erzhu Rong's staff.

sentences.zh: 榮性猛急，貴尤嚴峻，任使多愜榮心。

translations.literal: Rong's nature was fierce and impetuous; Gui was especially stern and severe, and in assignments and orders he often satisfied Rong's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was fierce and impetuous; Liu Gui was all the sterner and harsher, and in carrying out tasks he often pleased Rong.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，行汾州事，棄戍歸齊神武。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, he acted as head of Fen Prefecture affairs, abandoned his garrison post, and returned to Gao Huan of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era he governed Fen Prefecture, then abandoned his post and joined Gao Huan of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中尉、肆州大中正，加開府、西道行台僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Censor Director, Grand Rectifier of Si Prefecture, with added titles of Kaifu and Western Route Mobile Headquarters Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts—to Censor Director and grand rectifier of Si Prefecture—and was given the additional titles of kaifu noble and vice-director of the Western Route mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 貴所歷，莫不肆其威酷，非理殺害，視下如草芥。

translations.literal: Wherever Gui served, there was nowhere he did not unleash his might and cruelty; he killed people without just cause and regarded subordinates like grass and stubble.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held Liu Gui unleashed his cruelty, killing people without cause and treating those beneath him like chaff.

sentences.zh: 性峭直，攻訐無所回避。

translations.literal: His nature was severe and upright; in impeachment he avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright, he spared no one in his denunciations.

sentences.zh: 雖非佐命元功，然與神武布衣舊，特見親重。

translations.literal: Although he was not among the founding meritocrats, yet he had been an old companion of Gao Huan in plain cloth, and was especially shown intimacy and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though not among the founders of the dynasty, he had been an old friend of Gao Huan from their days in common dress, and was treated with special intimacy and regard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡忠武。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously given Grand Guardian, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, with posthumous name Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian and Duke of the Grand Commandant, with charge of recording the Masters of Writing; his posthumous name was Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，詔祭告其墓。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrificial announcement at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, an edict ordered sacrifices announced at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: During Huangjian, he was granted joint offering in the temple court of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangjian he was given a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 次子洪徽嗣樂縣男。

translations.literal: His second son Honghui succeeded to the baroncy of Le county.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Honghui inherited the title Baron of Le county.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都督、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously given Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made commander-in-chief and governor of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蔡俊，廣甯石門人也。

translations.literal: Cai Jun was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jun was from Shimen in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 父普，北方擾亂，走奔五原，守戰有功，拜甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: His father Pu, when the north was in turmoil, fled to rush to Wuyuan, had merit in garrison fighting, and was appointed General Who Tranquilizes the North.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pu, during the turmoil in the north, fled to Wuyuan, distinguished himself in defensive fighting, and was appointed General Who Tranquilizes the North.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈燕州刺史。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously given Governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made governor of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俊豪爽有膽略，齊神武微時，深相親附。

translations.literal: Jun was bold and generous and had courage and stratagem; when Gao Huan of Northern Qi was still obscure, they were deeply mutually intimate and attached.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jun was bold and daring; in Gao Huan of Northern Qi's early days they became close allies.

sentences.zh: 俊初為杜洛周所虜，時神武亦在洛周軍中。

translations.literal: Jun was at first taken captive by Du Luozhou; at that time Gao Huan was also in Luozhou's army.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jun was first captured by Du Luozhou, while Gao Huan too was then in Luozhou's ranks.

sentences.zh: 神武謀誅洛周，俊預其計。

translations.literal: Gao Huan plotted to kill Luozhou; Jun participated in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan plotted to kill Luozhou, Cai Jun took part in the scheme.

sentences.zh: 事泄奔葛榮。

translations.literal: When the affair leaked he fled to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed he fled to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 仍背榮歸爾硃榮。

translations.literal: He then turned his back on Rong and returned to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He then deserted Ge Rong and rejoined Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 從入洛。

translations.literal: He followed in entering Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及從破葛榮，平元顥，封烏洛縣男。

translations.literal: And when he followed in defeating Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wuluo county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the defeat of Ge Rong and the pacification of Yuan Hao and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuluo county.

sentences.zh: 隨神武舉義，及平鄴，破韓陵，並有戰功，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous cause, and when Ye was pacified and Hanling broken, he had merit in battle, and his nobility was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in his uprising; at the pacification of Ye and the victory at Hanling his military merit earned him promotion to marquis.

sentences.zh: 出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴暴，又多受納。

translations.literal: His governance was severe and violent, and he also took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was harsh and brutal, and he took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 然亦明解，有部分，吏人畏服之。

translations.literal: Yet he was also clear in understanding, had ability to assign duties, and officials and people feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was sharp-witted and knew how to assign duties; officials and commoners alike feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 性好賓客，頗稱施惠。

translations.literal: His nature loved entertaining guests, and he was rather said to dispense favors.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to host guests and was known for his generosity.

sentences.zh: 天平中，卒于揚州刺史，贈尚書令、司空公，諡曰威武。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he died in office as Governor of Yang Prefecture; posthumously given Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Minister of Works, posthumous name Martial and Mighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he died while serving as governor of Yang Prefecture; he was posthumously honored as Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Works, with the posthumous name Martial and Mighty.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，詔祭告其墓。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, an edict ordered sacrificial announcement at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, an edict ordered sacrifices announced at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享神武廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was granted joint offering in the temple court of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangjian he was given a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 韓賢，字普賢，廣甯石門人也。

translations.literal: Han Xian, styled Puxian, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, courtesy name Puxian, was from Shimen in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 壯健有武用。

translations.literal: Strong and healthy, he had martial usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Robust and skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 初，隨葛榮作逆，榮破後，爾硃榮擢充左右。

translations.literal: At first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion; after Rong was broken, Erzhu Rong selected him to fill his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed Ge Rong in revolt; after Ge Rong's defeat Erzhu Rong took him into his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 榮死，爾硃度律以賢為帳內都督，封汾陽縣伯。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Erzhu Dulü made Xian Commander-in-Chief of the Inner Tent, enfeoffing him Baron of Fenyang county.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death Erzhu Dulü appointed Han Xian commander of the inner guard and made him Baron of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 後為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later became governor of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武起義，度律以賢素為神武所知，恐有變，遣使征之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi raised the righteous cause, Dulü because Xian had long been known to Gao Huan, feared there would be a change, and sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi rose in revolt, Dulü, knowing that Han Xian had long been acquainted with Gao Huan and fearing defection, sent messengers to summon him.

sentences.zh: 不願去，乃密遣群蠻多舉烽，若有寇至。

translations.literal: Unwilling to leave, he secretly sent many of the tribal chiefs to raise beacon fires, as if bandits had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to go, he secretly had the tribal chiefs light many beacon fires as though invaders were at hand.

sentences.zh: 使者遂為啟，得停。

translations.literal: The envoys then made a report, and he obtained to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported the alarm and Han Xian was allowed to remain.

sentences.zh: 賢仍潛使人通誠于神武。

translations.literal: Xian still secretly sent men to express loyalty to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian still secretly sent envoys to pledge loyalty to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 後拜建州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed governor of Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天平初，為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was Governor of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianping he became governor of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人韓木蘭等起兵，賢破之。

translations.literal: The prefecture's Han Mulan and others raised troops; Xian defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Mulan and others of the prefecture rose in revolt, Han Xian defeated them.

sentences.zh: 親自案檢收甲仗，有一賊窘迫藏屍間，見將至，忽起斫賢，斷其脛而卒。

translations.literal: He personally examined and collected armor and weapons; one bandit, pressed hard, hid among corpses; seeing him about to arrive, he suddenly rose and hacked Xian, severed his shins, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: While personally inspecting captured arms and armor, he came upon a rebel who, cornered, had hidden among the corpses; when Han Xian approached the man leapt up and struck him, cutting off his legs, and Han Xian died.

sentences.zh: 始漢明帝時，西域以白馬負佛經送洛，因立白馬寺。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Ming of Han, the Western Regions sent Buddhist scriptures to Luoyang borne by a white horse, and thereby White Horse Temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: Since the reign of Emperor Ming of Han, Buddhist scriptures had been brought from the Western Regions to Luoyang on a white horse, and White Horse Temple was founded for them.

sentences.zh: 其經函傳於此寺，形制厚樸，世以古物，歷代寶之。

translations.literal: Its scripture cases were transmitted at this temple; their form was thick and plain, and the age regarded them as antiquities, treasured through successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The scripture cases had been kept at that temple—plain and massive—and had been treasured as antiquities through many dynasties.

sentences.zh: 賢知，故斫破之，未幾而死。

translations.literal: Xian knew of them, and therefore hacked and broke them; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian knew of them and deliberately smashed them; he died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 論者謂因此致禍。

translations.literal: Discussants said he brought disaster thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said his death was retribution for that act.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書令、司空。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子裔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited his position.

sentences.zh: 尉長命

translations.literal: Wei Zhangming
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhangming

sentences.zh: 尉長命，太安狄那人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhangming was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhangming was from Dina in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 父顯，魏代郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Xian was Administrator of Dai Commandery in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had been administrator of Dai Commandery under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 長命性和厚，有器識。

translations.literal: Zhangming's nature was gentle and thick, and he had capacity and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhangming was gentle and thoughtful, with a keen mind and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 參預齊神武起兵，破爾硃氏于韓陵，拜安南將軍。

translations.literal: He participated in Gao Huan of Northern Qi's raising troops, defeated the Erzhu clan at Hanling, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Gao Huan of Northern Qi's uprising, helped defeat the Erzhu at Hanling, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 樊子鵠據袞州反，除東南道大都督，與諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: Fan Zihu held Yan Prefecture in rebellion; he was appointed Grand Commander of the Southeast Route and with the various armies campaigned and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zihu rebelled and held Yan Prefecture, Wei Zhangming was appointed grand commander of the southeast route and, with the allied forces, suppressed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 徙幽州刺史，督安、平二州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of You Prefecture, supervising the two prefectures An and Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of You Prefecture with authority over An and Ping as well.

sentences.zh: 雖多聚斂，然以恩撫人，少得安集。

translations.literal: Although he gathered much exaction, yet by grace he comforted the people, and they were somewhat able to settle in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though he levied heavy taxes, he also treated the people with kindness, and they achieved a measure of stability.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰武壯。

translations.literal: On death posthumously given Minister of Works, posthumous name Martial and Robust.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works with the posthumous name Martial and Robust.

sentences.zh: 子興，字敬興。

translations.literal: His son Xing, styled Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing, courtesy name Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 便弓馬，有武藝，位冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Skilled at bow and horse, he had martial arts; his rank was General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Expert with bow and horse and skilled in arms, he rose to the rank of General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 王懷，字懷周，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Wang Huai, styled Huaizhou, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai, courtesy name Huaizhou, was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬，頗有氣尚。

translations.literal: In youth he loved bow and horse and had considerable martial spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved archery and horsemanship and had a spirited disposition.

sentences.zh: 隨齊神武于冀州起兵，討破爾硃兆于廣阿，又從破四胡何于韓陵，以功封盧鄉縣侯。

translations.literal: He followed Gao Huan of Northern Qi in raising troops at Ji Prefecture, campaigned and broke Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, and again followed in defeating the Four Hu at Hanling, and by merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Luxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan of Northern Qi in his uprising at Ji Prefecture, helped defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, and fought at Hanling against the coalition of the four Erzhu leaders, earning enfeoffment as Marquis of Luxiang.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為都督、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tianping he was Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he served as commander-in-chief and governor of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後從神武襲克西夏州。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan in a surprise attack that took Western Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Gao Huan in the surprise capture of Western Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還，為大都督，鎮下館。

translations.literal: On return, he was made Grand Commander, garrisoning Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made grand commander and posted to garrison Xiaoguan.

sentences.zh: 除車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Agile Cavalry with the privilege equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒公、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On death posthumously given Duke of Minister of Education and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Duke of the Minister of Education and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 懷以武藝勳誠，為神武所知。

translations.literal: Huai, by his martial arts merit and loyalty, was known to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huai's martial skill and loyal service won Gao Huan's esteem.

sentences.zh: 志力未申，論者惜其不遂。

translations.literal: His will and strength were not fully expressed; discussants regretted that he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His ambitions were never fully realized, and many lamented that his promise went unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配饗神武廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, granted joint offering at Gao Huan's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangjian he was given a place in the offerings at Gao Huan's temple.

sentences.zh: 子胄，性輕俠，頗敏慧，少在神武左右。

translations.literal: His son Zhou, nature light and chivalrous, rather clever, in youth was at Gao Huan's left and right.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou was rakish and clever and in his youth served at Gao Huan's side.

sentences.zh: 天平中，擢為東郡太守。

translations.literal: During Tianping he was promoted to Administrator of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was promoted to administrator of Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 家本豐財，又多聚斂，動極豪華；

translations.literal: His family was originally rich in wealth, and he also gathered much exaction, his movements extremely luxurious;
translations.idiomatic: His family was already wealthy, and he exacted still more; his way of life was extravagantly lavish;

sentences.zh: 賓客往來，將迎至厚。

translations.literal: Guests coming and going, he received and escorted with utmost generosity.
translations.idiomatic: and he entertained visitors with the greatest hospitality.

sentences.zh: 興和未，神武攻王壁還，留清河公嶽為行台，鎮守晉州，以胄隸之。

translations.literal: Late in Xinghe, Gao Huan returned from attacking Wangbi, left Prince of Qinghe Yue as mobile headquarters, garrisoning Jin Prefecture, and attached Zhou subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xinghe, when Gao Huan returned from the siege of Wangbi, he left Prince Yue of Qinghe as mobile headquarters commander to hold Jin Prefecture, with Zhou under his command.

sentences.zh: 胄飲酒遊縱，不勤防守，神武責之。

translations.literal: Zhou drank wine and wandered freely, not diligent in defense; Gao Huan reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou drank and caroused and neglected the defense; Gao Huan reprimanded him.

sentences.zh: 懼，遂潛遣使送款于周。

translations.literal: In fear, he then secretly sent envoys to deliver allegiance to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, he secretly sent envoys to offer his allegiance to Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 為人所糾，推勘未得實，神武特免之。

translations.literal: He was impeached by someone; investigation and examination did not obtain proof; Gao Huan specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported him, but the investigation found no proof and Gao Huan personally pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 胄內不自安，乃與儀同爾硃文暢、參軍房子遠、鄭仲禮等陰圖弑逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhou inwardly was not at ease, and then with Yitong Erzhu Wenchang, Staff Officer Fang Ziyuan, Zheng Zhongli, and others secretly plotted regicide; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his heart, Zhou joined Yitong Erzhu Wenchang, staff officer Fang Ziyuan, Zheng Zhongli, and others in a secret plot of assassination and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 莫多婁貸文

translations.literal: Moduoluo Daiwen
translations.idiomatic: Moduoluo Daiwen

sentences.zh: 莫多婁貸文，太安狄那人也。

translations.literal: Moduoluo Daiwen was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Moduoluo Daiwen was from Dina in Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 驍果有膽氣。

translations.literal: Fierce and stalwart, he had courage and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and fearless in battle.

sentences.zh: 從神武起兵，破爾硃兆于廣阿，封石城縣子。

translations.literal: Following Gao Huan in raising troops, he broke Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was enfeoffed Viscount of Shicheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in his uprising, helped defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 從破四胡于韓陵，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking the Four Hu at Hanling and advanced his nobility to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Hanling against the Erzhu coalition and was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 從平爾硃兆於赤谼嶺，兆自縊，貸文獲其屍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Erzhu Zhao at Chikong Ridge; Zhao hanged himself, and Daiwen obtained his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Chikong Ridge; when Zhao hanged himself Daiwen recovered his body.

sentences.zh: 天平中，進爵為公，晉州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tianping he advanced his nobility to duke and was Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping he was promoted to duke and appointed governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元象初，除車騎大將軍、儀同三司、南道大都督，與行台侯景攻獨孤信于金墉城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Grand Commander of the South Route; with mobile headquarters Hou Jing he attacked Dugu Xin at Jinyong city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanxiang he was made General of the Agile Cavalry, honored equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and grand commander of the southern route; with mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing he besieged Dugu Xin at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 周文帝出函谷，景與高昂議待其至。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou came out through Hangu Pass; Jing and Gao Ang discussed waiting for his arrival.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Wen of Zhou marched out through Hangu Pass, Hou Jing and Gao Ang debated waiting for him to arrive.

sentences.zh: 貸文請率所部擊其前鋒，景等固不許。

translations.literal: Daiwen requested to lead his division to strike their vanguard; Jing and the others firmly did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen asked to lead his troops against the enemy vanguard, but Hou Jing and the others firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 貸文性勇而專，不受命，以輕騎一千，軍前斥堠，死于周軍。

translations.literal: Daiwen's nature was brave and self-willed; not accepting orders, with a thousand light cavalry he served as advance scout before the army and died in Zhou's army.
translations.idiomatic: Impetuous and willful, he disobeyed orders and rode forward with a thousand light horsemen to reconnoiter; he was killed by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書左僕射、司徒公。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 子敬顯嗣，強直勤幹，少以武力見知。

translations.literal: His son Jingxian succeeded; upright and strong, diligent and capable, in youth he was known by martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxian inherited his title—a stern, diligent man who won notice in his youth for his military prowess.

sentences.zh: 恆從斛律光征討，數有戰功。

translations.literal: He constantly followed Hulu Guang in campaigns; many times he had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He often followed Hulu Guang on campaign and won repeated distinctions in battle.

sentences.zh: 光每令敬顯前驅置營，中夜巡察，或達旦不眠。

translations.literal: Guang every time ordered Jingxian to ride ahead and set camp; at midnight he patrolled, sometimes until dawn without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Guang regularly sent Jingxian ahead to pitch camp; he patrolled at midnight and sometimes went without sleep until dawn.

sentences.zh: 臨敵置陣，亦命部分將士，深見重。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy in setting battle array, he also ordered assigning portions of officers and soldiers, and was deeply valued.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he also directed the disposition of troops and was held in deep esteem.

sentences.zh: 位至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His rank reached Kaifu Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of kaifu with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 武平七年，從後主平陽敗歸，在并州與唐邕等推立安德王稱尊號。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuping, he followed the Later Ruler in defeat returning from Pingyang, and at Bing Prefecture with Tang Yong and others pushed to establish Prince of Ande to proclaim the honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuping, after the defeat at Pingyang, he returned with the emperor to Bing Prefecture and joined Tang Yong and others in raising Prince Ande to the throne.

sentences.zh: 安德敗，武將皆投周軍，唯敬顯走還鄴，授司徒。

translations.literal: Prince Ande was defeated; military commanders all submitted to the Zhou army; only Jingxian fled back to Ye and was appointed Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ande's cause collapsed, the generals one after another went over to the Northern Zhou armies; Jingxian alone escaped back to Ye, where he was made Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平鄴，執之，斬於閶闔門外，責其不留晉陽也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Ye, seized him, and executed him outside the Chuanghe Gate, blaming him for not remaining at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou took Ye, he had Jingxian arrested and beheaded outside the Chuanghe Gate, condemning him for abandoning Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 厙狄迴洛

translations.literal: Shedi Huiluo
translations.idiomatic: Shedi Huiluo

sentences.zh: 厙狄回洛，代人也。

translations.literal: Shedi Huiluo was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Shedi Huiluo came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有武力，儀貌魁偉。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial prowess; his bearing was towering.
translations.idiomatic: He showed martial talent from his youth and cut a towering figure.

sentences.zh: 初事爾硃榮。

translations.literal: At first he served Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the service of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮死，隸爾硃兆。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he came under Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death he followed Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 神武舉兵於信都，回洛擁眾來歸。

translations.literal: Gao Huan raised troops at Xindu; Huiluo led the masses to submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised his banner at Xindu, Huiluo brought his followers over to join him.

sentences.zh: 從破四胡于韓陵，以軍功封順陽縣子，累遷夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating the Four Hu at Hanling; for military merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shunyang County, and was promoted through posts to Governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the crushing defeat of the Erzhu faction at Hanling, earned enfeoffment as Viscount of Shunyang for his battlefield service, and rose step by step to governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 昭帝即位，封順陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shunyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao made him Prince of Shunyang upon his accession.

sentences.zh: 大寧初，為朔州刺史，轉太子太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daning, he was Governor of Shuo Province; he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daning era he governed Shuo Province, then became Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; they posthumously granted Grand Commandant and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 厙狄盛

translations.literal: Shedi Sheng
translations.idiomatic: Shedi Sheng

sentences.zh: 厙狄盛，字安盛，懷朔人也。

translations.literal: Shedi Sheng, style name Ansheng, was a native of Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shedi Sheng, courtesy name Ansheng, was born at Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 性和柔，少有武用。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and yielding; in youth he had martial usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by temperament, he nevertheless possessed military skill from an early age.

sentences.zh: 初為神武親信都督，從征伐。

translations.literal: At first he was Gao Huan's trusted chief commander and followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a trusted personal commander in Gao Huan's entourage and followed him on campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 累遷幽州刺史，封長廣縣公。

translations.literal: He was promoted through posts to Governor of You Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Changguang County.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became governor of You Province and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，改封華陽縣公，後拜特進。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his fief was changed to Duke of Huayang County; later he was appointed Special Advanced.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded he was transferred to the ducal title of Huayang and later named Special Advanced.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉公。

translations.literal: He died; they posthumously granted Grand Commandant Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously elevated to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 張保洛

translations.literal: Zhang Baoluo
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoluo

sentences.zh: 張保洛，自雲本出南陽西鄂，家世好賓客，尚氣俠，頗為北土所知。

translations.literal: Zhang Baoluo—from birth his lineage traced to Xihuan of Nanyang; for generations his house loved guests, prized chivalrous spirit, and was widely known in the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoluo's family originally hailed from Xihuan in Nanyang; they had entertained guests for generations and cultivated a reputation for bravado that was well known across the north.

sentences.zh: 保洛少便弓馬。

translations.literal: Baoluo in youth was adept with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Baoluo mastered bow and saddle while still young.

sentences.zh: 初從葛榮。

translations.literal: At first he followed Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He first rode with Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，仍為爾硃榮統軍。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, he then served as Erzhu Rong's unit commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat he became a regiment commander under Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 後隸齊神武。

translations.literal: Later he came under Qi Divine Martial Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武起兵，保洛為帳內，從破爾硃兆于廣阿及韓陵戰。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised troops, Baoluo was within the tent staff; he followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and the battle at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised his army, Baoluo served in his personal guard and fought at Guang'a and Hanling in the overthrow of Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 元象初，為西夏州刺史，以前後功，封安武縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was Governor of Western Xia Province; for former and later merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Anwu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang he was made governor of Western Xia Province and, for his accumulated service, enfeoffed as Baron of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 又從戰芒山，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Again he followed in battle at Mangshan and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Mangshan and was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣事，曆梁州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Wenxiang succeeded the enterprise; he served as Governor of Liang Province and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gao Cheng he served as governor of Liang Province and was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，加開府，仍為刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Grand Preliminary Guard was added; he still was governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne he was made a Grand Guardian of the Household while retaining his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 聚斂，為百姓所患。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth; he was the trouble of common people.
translations.idiomatic: He extorted the people and became a plague upon them.

sentences.zh: 濟南初，兼侍中，尋出為滄州刺史，封敷城郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jinan, he was concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he went out as Governor of Cang Province and was enfeoffed as Prince of Fucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jinan reign he was named Attendant-in-Ordinary, then sent out as governor of Cang Province and enfeoffed as Prince of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 以聚斂免官，奪王爵。

translations.literal: For amassing wealth he was removed from office and stripped of princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: His extortion cost him his offices and his princely title.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈前官，追復本封。

translations.literal: He died; they granted his former offices and restored his original enfeoffment posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his former posts were restored and his original title reinstated.

sentences.zh: 從神武出山東，又有賀拔仁、曲珍、段琛、尉摽、子相貴、康得、韓建業、封輔相、范舍樂、牒舍樂，並以軍功至大官，史失其事。

translations.literal: Those who followed Gao Huan east out of the mountains also included Heluoren, Qu Zhen, Duan Chen, Wei Biao, Zi Xianggui, Kang De, Han Jianye, Feng Fuxiang, Fan Shele, Die Shele—all reached great offices by military merit; the histories have lost their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Among the men who followed Gao Huan east into Shandong were Heluoren, Qu Zhen, Duan Chen, Wei Biao, Zi Xianggui, Kang De, Han Jianye, Feng Fuxiang, Fan Shele, and Die Shele, all of whom rose to high office through military service; the histories no longer record their deeds in detail.

sentences.zh: 仁字天惠，無善人。

translations.literal: Ren's style name was Tianhui; he had no virtuous man.
translations.idiomatic: Heluoren, style name Tianhui, was no virtuous soul.

sentences.zh: 以帳內都督從神武破爾硃氏于韓陵，力戰有功。

translations.literal: As chief commander within the tent he followed Gao Huan in defeating the Erzhu clan at Hanling; fighting hard he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander of Gao Huan's personal guard he fought at Hanling in the destruction of the Erzhu house and distinguished himself in fierce combat.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封安定郡王，歷數州刺史、太保、太師、右丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anding Commandery; he served through posts as several provinces' governor, Grand Guardian, Grand Tutor, Right Chancellor, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was made Prince of Anding and rose through governorships of several provinces to Grand Guardian, Grand Tutor, Right Chancellor, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 武平元年薨，贈假黃鉞、相國、太尉、錄尚書、十二州諸軍事、朔州刺史，諡曰武。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he died; they posthumously granted the ceremonial yellow axe, Chancellor of State, Grand Commandant, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, military affairs over twelve provinces, Governor of Shuo Province—posthumous title Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Wuping and was posthumously invested with the golden axe, the title of Chancellor of State and Grand Commandant, supervisory authority over the Masters of Writing and twelve provinces' military affairs, and the governorship of Shuo; his posthumous name was Wu, "the Martial."

sentences.zh: 珍字舍洛，西平酒泉人。

translations.literal: Zhen's style name was Sheluo; he was a man of Jiuquan, Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhen, style name Sheluo, came from Jiuquan in Xiping.

sentences.zh: 壯勇騎射，以帳內從神武。

translations.literal: Strong and brave at mounted archery; he followed Gao Huan within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful mounted archer, he rode with Gao Huan in his personal following.

sentences.zh: 天統中，封安康郡王。

translations.literal: In the Tian Tong era he was enfeoffed Prince of Ankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiantong era he was created Prince of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 武平初，為豫州道行台尚書令、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was Commander-in-Chief Secretariat Director on the Yuzhou route and Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuping he headed the Secretariat of the Yuzhou military administration and governed Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died; they posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 琛字懷寶，代人。

translations.literal: Chen's style name was Huaibao; he was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chen, courtesy name Huaibao, was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有武用，從起兵。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial usefulness; he followed in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in arms from youth, he joined Gao Huan when the army was first raised.

sentences.zh: 天保中，開府儀同三司、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era: Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he held the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and governed Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 摽，代人，大寧初，位司徒，封海昌王。

translations.literal: Biao was a native of Dai; at the beginning of Daning he held the post of Grand Steward and was enfeoffed Prince of Haichang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Biao, a man of Dai, became Grand Steward and Prince of Haichang early in the Daning era.

sentences.zh: 卒，子相貴嗣。

translations.literal: He died; Zi Xianggui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was succeeded by Zi Xianggui.

sentences.zh: 相貴，武平末，開府儀同三司、晉州道行台尚書僕射、晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianggui: at the end of Wuping, Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Jinzhou route administration, Governor of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Wuping, Xianggui held the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household with parity to the Three Excellencies, served as vice director of the Jinzhou route Secretariat, and governed Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 及行台左丞侯子欽等密啟周武帝請師，求為內應。

translations.literal: When the route administration's Left Assistant Director Hou Ziqin and others secretly memorialized Emperor Wu of Zhou to request troops, seeking to be internal collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou's left assistant director Hou Ziqin and others secretly appealed to Emperor Wu of Zhou to send troops, offering themselves as allies within the walls.

sentences.zh: 周武自率眾至城下。

translations.literal: Zhou Martial himself led the masses to below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou personally led his army to the walls of Jin.

sentences.zh: 子欽等夜開城門，引軍入，鎖相貴送長安，卒。

translations.literal: Ziqin and others at night opened the city gates, led the army in, chained Xianggui and sent him to Chang'an; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqin and his fellows opened the gates by night, admitted the Zhou troops, put Xianggui in chains and sent him to Chang'an, where he died.

sentences.zh: 弟相願，強幹有膽略，武平末，開府儀同三司、領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xiangyuan: strong and capable with daring and strategy; at the end of Wuping, Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Army Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiangyuan was a forceful man of courage and design; at the end of Wuping he too held the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household and served as Army Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 自平陽至并州及到鄴，每立計將殺高阿那肱，廢後主立廣甯王。

translations.literal: From Pingyang to Bing Province and on reaching Ye, every time he devised plans intending to kill Gao Anagong, depose the Later Ruler and install the Prince of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: From Pingyang through Bingzhou to Ye, he repeatedly plotted to kill Gao Anagong, depose the emperor, and set Prince Guangning on the throne.

sentences.zh: 事竟不果。

translations.literal: The affair in the end did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: None of these designs ever came off.

sentences.zh: 及廣寧被出，相願拔佩刀斫柱而歎曰：「大事去矣，知復何言！」

translations.literal: When Guangning was driven out, Xiangyuan drew his belt knife and hacked a pillar, sighing: "The great affair is gone—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guangning was removed from court, Xiangyuan drew his sword and struck a pillar, crying, "The great matter is lost—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 德，代人。

translations.literal: De was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kang De was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 歷數州刺史、並省尚書左僕射、開府儀同三司，封新蔡王。

translations.literal: He served through posts as several provinces' governor, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing of the Bing province office, Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies; enfeoffed Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He governed several provinces in turn, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing for Bing province, and was ultimately created Prince of Xincai with the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household.

sentences.zh: 建業、輔相，俱不知所從來。

translations.literal: Jianye and Fuxiang—both are not known whence they came.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jianye and Feng Fuxiang—nothing is recorded of their origins.

sentences.zh: 建業位領軍大將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Jianye held the post of Army Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye served as Army Commander-in-Chief and governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 以輔相為朔州總管。

translations.literal: Fuxiang was made Commander-in-chief of Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang was appointed overall commander of Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 范舍樂，代人。

translations.literal: Fan Shele was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shele came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 有武藝，筋力絕人。

translations.literal: He had martial arts; muscle strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in arms, his raw strength was beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 位東雍州刺史、開府儀同三司，封平舒侯。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Eastern Yong Province, Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies; enfeoffed Marquis of Pingshu.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Eastern Yong Province, held the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingshu.

sentences.zh: 牒舍樂，武威人。

translations.literal: Die Shele was a man of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Die Shele was from Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、營州刺史，封漢中郡公，戰歿關中。

translations.literal: Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Governor of Ying Province; enfeoffed Duke of Hanzhong Commandery; died in battle in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian of the Household and governor of Ying Province, he was created Duke of Hanzhong and fell in battle in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳相

translations.literal: Houmo Chenxiang
translations.idiomatic: Houmo Chenxiang

sentences.zh: 次子晉貴，嚴重有文武幹略，襲爵白水王，武衛將軍、開府儀同三司、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Second son Jingui: grave and weighty with civil and military capacity and strategy; he inherited the title Prince of Baishui, Martial Guard General, Grand Preliminary Guard with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jingui was a man of sober bearing and real ability in civil and military affairs; he inherited the princely title of Baishui, served as Martial Guard General and governor of Liang Province, and held the rank of Grand Guardian of the Household.

sentences.zh: 歸周，授上大將軍，封信安縣公。

translations.literal: He submitted to Zhou; they appointed him Grand General, enfeoffed him Duke of Xin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When he went over to Zhou he was named Grand General and enfeoffed Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 子仲宣，太常丞。

translations.literal: Son Zhongxuan: Director under the Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongxuan served as a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子弘穎、弘信，雍州司士參軍。

translations.literal: Sons Hongying and Hongxin: Military Staff Registrar of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Hongying and Hongxin held staff posts in the Yongzhou command.

sentences.zh: 子行方、行儉、行恭。

translations.literal: Sons Xingfang, Xingjian, Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xingfang, Xingjian, and Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 薛孤延

translations.literal: Xue Guyan
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guyan

sentences.zh: 薛孤延，代人也。

translations.literal: Xue Guyan was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guyan came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少驍果，從神武起兵，以功累加儀同三司。

translations.literal: In youth bold and decisive; he followed Gao Huan in raising troops; for merit he was repeatedly promoted to Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and resolute in his youth, he joined Gao Huan at the founding of the army and rose through repeated promotions to ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 從西征，至蒲津。

translations.literal: He followed the western expedition to Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on the western campaign as far as Pujin.

sentences.zh: 及竇泰失利，神武班師，延後殿，且戰且行，一日斫折十五刀。

translations.literal: When Dou Tai suffered defeat, Gao Huan withdrew the army; Yan covered the rear, fighting while marching; in one day he hewed through fifteen blades.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Tai's army was broken, Gao Huan ordered the retreat and Guyan took the rear guard, fighting as he withdrew; in a single day he shattered fifteen swords.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗閱馬於北牧，道逢暴雨，大雷震地，火燒浮圖。

translations.literal: Gao Huan once inspected horses at the northern pastures; on the road they met violent rain; great thunder shook the earth; fire burned the stupa.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was once reviewing horses at the northern pastures when a sudden storm broke; thunder shook the ground and lightning set a stupa ablaze.

sentences.zh: 神武令延視之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan ordered Yan to go view it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Guyan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 延案槊直前，大呼繞浮圖走，火遂滅。

translations.literal: Yan braced his lance and went straight forward, shouting greatly as he ran around the stupa; the fire then extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan couched his spear and charged straight ahead, shouting as he circled the burning stupa—and the fire went out.

sentences.zh: 延還，須及馬鬃尾皆焦。

translations.literal: When Yan returned, his beard and the horse's mane and tail were all scorched.
translations.idiomatic: When he rode back, both his whiskers and his horse's mane and tail had been singed black.

sentences.zh: 神武歎其勇決，曰：「延乃能與霹靂鬥！」

translations.literal: Gao Huan sighed at his brave decisiveness, saying: "Yan can actually fight with thunderbolts!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan marveled at his daring. "Guyan can do battle with the thunder itself!" he said.

sentences.zh: 後封平秦公，與諸將討潁川。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingqin and with the generals campaigned against Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was created Duke of Pingqin and joined the generals in the siege of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 延專監造土山，以酒醉，為敵所襲據。

translations.literal: Yan exclusively supervised building the earthen mount; because of drunkenness on wine, the enemy raided and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan was put in charge of building the siege mound but, drunk on wine, let the enemy seize it in a night attack.

sentences.zh: 潁川平，諸將還京師，宴華林園。

translations.literal: When Yingchuan was pacified, the generals returned to the capital and feasted in the Huangling Garden.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingchuan fell, the commanders returned to the capital for a feast in the Hualin Gardens.

sentences.zh: 文襄啟魏帝，坐延階下以辱之。

translations.literal: Wenxiang memorialized the Wei Emperor to seat Yan below the steps to humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng asked the Wei emperor to seat Guyan below the hall steps as a public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，別賜爵都昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, they separately granted the title Duke of Duchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi was founded he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 延性好酒，率多昏醉。

translations.literal: Yan's nature loved wine; mostly he was dazed in drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan loved his wine and was as often drunk as sober.

sentences.zh: 以善戰，每大軍征討，常為前鋒。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled at battle, every time the great army campaigned he was often the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he fought so well that on every major campaign he was placed in the van.

sentences.zh: 位太子太保、太傅。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 斛律羌舉

translations.literal: Hulu Qiangju
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Qiangju

sentences.zh: 斛律羌舉，太安人也。

translations.literal: Hulu Qiangju was a native of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Qiangju came from Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 世為部落酋長。

translations.literal: For generations they were tribal chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had led their tribe for generations.

sentences.zh: 羌舉少驍果，從爾硃兆。

translations.literal: Qiangju in youth was bold and decisive; he followed Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangju was fierce and resolute in his youth and served under Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆破，乃歸誠神武。

translations.literal: When Zhao was broken, he then returned in sincerity to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was destroyed he submitted in good faith to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武以其忠於所事，亦加嗟賞。

translations.literal: Gao Huan because of his loyalty to the matter he served also added sighs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan admired his loyalty to whichever master he served and spoke of him with evident respect.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除大都督。
