translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was appointed Grand Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was named Grand Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 後從神武戰于沙苑，時議進趣計，羌舉曰：「黑獺若欲固守，無糧援可恃。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan in battle at Shayuan; at the time they deliberated on advance plans; Qiangju said: "If Black Badger wishes to hold firm, no grain support can be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning with Gao Huan at Shayuan, he took part in the council on how to advance. "If Heiba intends to stand on the defensive," Qiangju said, "he has no supplies he can count on.

sentences.zh: 今揣其情，欲一死決，有同狾犬，或能噬人。

translations.literal: Now I gauge their feeling: they wish one death's decision; it is like a mad dog—it may be able to bite men.
translations.idiomatic: But I read their mood now as readiness to fight to the death—they are like cornered curs and may yet bite.

sentences.zh: 且渭曲土濘，無所用力。

translations.literal: Moreover at Weiqu the soil is muddy; nowhere to exert force.
translations.idiomatic: And the ground at Weiqu is boggy—nowhere for our strength to tell.

sentences.zh: 若不與戰，徑趣咸陽，咸陽空虛，可不戰而克。

translations.literal: If we do not give battle but go straight to hurry to Xianyang, Xianyang is empty and weak; we can take it without battle.
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse battle and march straight on Xianyang, that city stands hollow—we can seize it without a fight.

sentences.zh: 拔其根本，則黑獺之首，可懸軍門。」

translations.literal: Pull up their root, then Black Badger's head can be hung at the army gate."
translations.idiomatic: Strike at their root, and Heiba's head may yet hang from our gate.

sentences.zh: 神武欲縱火焚之，侯景曰：「當禽以示百姓，燒殺誰復信之？」

translations.literal: Gao Huan wished to set fire and burn them; Hou Jing said: "We ought to capture them alive to show the people—if we burn and kill, who will believe us again?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wanted to burn them where they stood, but Hou Jing objected: "Take them alive and show the people. Burn and slaughter them, and who will ever trust us again?"

sentences.zh: 諸將議既有異同，遂戰于渭曲，大軍敗績。

translations.literal: The generals' deliberations already had differing views; they then battled at Weiqu, and the great army suffered a routed record.
translations.idiomatic: The counsels of the commanders were divided, so they gave battle at Weiqu after all—and the main army met utter disaster.

sentences.zh: 後封密縣侯，為東夏州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed Marquis of Mi County and made Inspector of Eastern Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as Marquis of Mi and appointed inspector of Eastern Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 有疫疾，刺胸，竹筒吮之，垂愈。

translations.literal: He had an epidemic illness; they pierced his chest and sucked with bamboo tubes—he was nearly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When plague struck him, physicians pierced his chest and drew out the pus with bamboo tubes; he was on the verge of recovery.

sentences.zh: 因怒，創裂而卒。

translations.literal: Through anger, the wound split open and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In a fit of rage the wound tore open again, and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 子孝卿嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaojing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaojing succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 斛律孝卿

translations.literal: Hulu Xiaojing
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Xiaojing

sentences.zh: 孝卿少聰敏，機悟有風檢。

translations.literal: Xiaojing in youth was bright and clever, quick-witted with moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojing was clever and quick-minded from boyhood, with a keen wit and a sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 武平末，位侍中、開府儀同三司，封義甯王，知內省事，典外兵、騎兵機密。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he held the posts of Palace Attendant and Opening Office with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, was enfeoffed Prince of Yining, oversaw inner-palace affairs, and managed outer troops and cavalry secrets.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he was palace attendant and held an opening office with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, was created Prince of Yining, oversaw inner-palace business, and held charge of field armies and the cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 時政由群豎，自趙彥深死後，朝貴典機密者，唯孝卿一人差居雅道，不至貪穢。

translations.literal: At the time government was in the hands of the petty men; after Zhao Yanshen died, among court nobles who held secrets, only Xiaojing alone stood somewhat in the refined way and did not reach greed and filth.
translations.idiomatic: Power then lay with the eunuch cabal; after Zhao Yanshen's death, of the great courtiers who held state secrets, Xiaojing alone still walked a measure of the high road and did not sink into greed and corruption.

sentences.zh: 後主至齊州，以孝卿為尚書令，又以中書侍郎薛道衡為侍中，封北海王。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord reached Qizhou, he made Xiaojing Director of the Masters of Writing, and also made Secretariat Gentleman Xue Daoheng Palace Attendant and Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord reached Qizhou, he appointed Xiaojing director of the Masters of Writing and made secretariat gentleman Xue Daoheng palace attendant and Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 二人勸後主作承光詔，禪位任城王。

translations.literal: The two urged the Later Lord to issue the Chengguang edict, abdicating the throne to the Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: The two urged the Later Lord to draw up the Chengguang abdication edict and yield the throne to the Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 令孝卿齎詔策及傳國璽往瀛州，孝卿便詣鄴。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiaojing to carry the edict protocols and the dynastic seal to Yingzhou; Xiaojing went straight to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiaojing to Yingzhou with the abdication documents and the imperial seal, but Xiaojing went straight on to Ye instead.

sentences.zh: 仍從周武帝入關，授儀同大將軍、宣納上士。

translations.literal: Still he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou through the Pass and was appointed Grand General with Pomp Equal Rank and Xuan-nabe Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Emperor Wu of Zhou through the Pass and was made grand general with ceremonial parity and Xuan-nabe senior gentleman.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，位太府卿、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In Sui Kaihuang he held the posts of Grand Treasurer and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he served as grand treasurer and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 張瓊，字連德，代人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiong, style name Liande, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiong, whose style was Liande, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少壯健，有武用，初隨葛榮為亂。

translations.literal: In youth he was strong and robust, with martial utility; at first he followed Ge Rong in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Robust and warlike in his youth, he first followed Ge Rong in revolt.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，爾硃榮以為都督。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, Erzhu Rong made him a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was crushed, Erzhu Rong appointed him a military commander.

sentences.zh: 後歷位濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the post of Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃氏敗，歸神武，拜滄州刺史，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan was defeated, he returned to Gao Huan, was appointed Inspector of Cang Province, and was additionally made Rapid-as-Lightning Grand General and Opening Office with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu house fell, he submitted to Gao Huan, was named inspector of Cang Province, and was further promoted to rapid-cavalry grand general with an opening office and ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 天平中，神武襲克夏州，以瓊為慰勞大使，留鎮之。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era Gao Huan stormed and took Xia Province; he made Qiong consolation-and-reward envoy and left him to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping, after Gao Huan stormed and took Xia Province, he made Qiong commissioner to comfort the region and left him to hold the garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋為周文帝所陷，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was trapped by Duke Wen of Zhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon trapped by Duke Wen of Zhou and died.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒、都督、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Education, commander, and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of education, commander-in-chief, and inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 瓊子欣，尚魏平陽公主，除駙馬都尉、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、建州刺史，南鄭伯。

translations.literal: Qiong's son Xin married the Princess of Pingyang of Wei; he was appointed Commandant of the Horse for the Imperial Son-in-Law, Rapid-as-Lightning Grand General, Opening Office with Pomp Equal to Three Excellencies, Inspector of Jian Province, and Baron of Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's son Xin married the Princess of Pingyang of Wei and was made commandant of the horse for the imperial son-in-law, rapid-cavalry grand general, holder of an opening office with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, inspector of Jian Province, and Baron of Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 瓊常憂其太盛，每謂親識曰：「凡人官爵，莫若處中。

translations.literal: Qiong often worried that his rank was too lofty; every time he told close acquaintances: "For a man's offices and titles, nothing is better than standing in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong often fretted that the boy had risen too high and would tell friends, "For any man, rank is safest in the middle.

sentences.zh: 欣位秩太高，深為憂慮。」

translations.literal: Xin's position and rank were too high; he was deeply worried."
translations.idiomatic: Xin's posts sit too high—that is what gnaws at me.

sentences.zh: 而欣豪險，遂與公主情好不篤。

translations.literal: But Xin was arrogant and dangerous, and so his affection with the princess was not close.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xin was proud and reckless, and his bond with the princess grew cold.

sentences.zh: 尋為孝武所害。

translations.literal: Soon he was harmed by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Xiaowu had him killed.

sentences.zh: 時人稱瓊先見。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised Qiong's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day said Qiong had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 宋顯，字仲華，敦煌效穀人也。

translations.literal: Song Xian, style name Zhonghua, was a native of Xiaogu in Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Xian, whose style was Zhonghua, came from Xiaogu in Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 性果毅，有幹用。

translations.literal: His nature was bold and resolute; he had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was resolute by nature and capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 初事爾硃榮，稍遷為記室參軍。

translations.literal: At first he served Erzhu Rong and was gradually promoted to staff adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Erzhu Rong and was gradually promoted to staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 榮死，世隆等以為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shilong and the others made him Inspector of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death, Shilong and his faction appointed him inspector of Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 後歸神武為行台左丞，拜西袞州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Gao Huan as left aide of the executive agency and was appointed Inspector of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted to Gao Huan as left director of the executive agency and was named inspector of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 在州多所受納，然勇決有氣幹，檢禦左右，咸得其心力。

translations.literal: In the province he accepted many bribes, yet he was brave, decisive, and possessed force of character; in inspecting and controlling those around him, he won all their hearts and effort.
translations.idiomatic: In office he took many bribes, yet he was bold, decisive, and full of drive; he kept his subordinates in hand and won their wholehearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及河陰之戰，深入，沒於行陣。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin he went deep in and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin he pressed deep into the enemy line and fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Duke Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of education.

sentences.zh: 王則，字元軌，自雲太原人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ze, style name Yuangui, claimed to be a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze, whose style was Yuangui, claimed descent from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少驍果，有武藝。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and decisive, with martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and resolute in his youth, he was skilled in arms.

sentences.zh: 初隨叔父魏廣平內史老生征討，每有戰功。

translations.literal: At first he followed his uncle, Wei's interior secretary of Guangping, Laosheng, on campaigns; every time there was merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned with his uncle Laosheng, interior secretary of Guangping under Wei, and won merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 老生為朝廷所知，則頗有力。

translations.literal: Laosheng became known to the court; Ze had considerable influence.
translations.idiomatic: When Laosheng came to the court's notice, Ze's standing rose with his.

sentences.zh: 初以軍功賜白水子。

translations.literal: At first for military merit he was granted the title Viscount of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: His first reward for military merit was the title Viscount of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，則與老生俱降顥。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Ze and Laosheng together surrendered to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Ze and Laosheng surrendered to him together.

sentences.zh: 顥疑老生，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Hao suspected Laosheng and then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao grew suspicious of Laosheng and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 則奔廣州刺史鄭先護，與同拒顥。

translations.literal: Ze fled to Inspector of Guang Province Zheng Xianhu and with him resisted Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Ze fled to Zheng Xianhu, inspector of Guang Province, and with him held out against Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，為東徐州防城都督。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, he became commander of the eastern Xuzhou garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao's defeat he was made commander of the eastern Xuzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死也，東徐州刺史斛斯椿是其枝黨，內懷憂懼。

translations.literal: At Erzhu Rong's death, the Inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, Husichun, was of his branch faction and inwardly harbored worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Husichun, inspector of eastern Xuzhou and a member of his faction, was inwardly shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 時梁立魏汝南王悅為魏主，資其士馬，送之境上，椿遂降悅。

translations.literal: At the time Liang set up Wei's Prince of Runan, Yue, as ruler of Wei, supplied his soldiers and horses, and sent them to the border; Husichun then surrendered to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had installed Yuan Yue, Prince of Runan, as a rival Wei sovereign and was sending him troops and horses to the frontier; Husichun thereupon went over to Yue.

sentences.zh: 則與蘭陵太守李義擊其偏師，破之。

translations.literal: Ze with the Administrator of Lanling, Li Yi, struck their detached division and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Li Yi, administrator of Lanling, attacked Yue's flank force and routed it.

sentences.zh: 魏因以則行北徐州事，隸爾硃仲遠。

translations.literal: Wei thereupon had Ze act in northern Xuzhou affairs, subordinate to Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then put Ze in charge of northern Xuzhou under Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 仲遠敗，乃歸神武。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan was defeated, he then returned to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyuan fell, he submitted to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 天平初，頻以軍功，都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, repeatedly for military merit he became commander and Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianping, through repeated battlefield merit, he became commander and inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 則有威武，邊人畏伏之。

translations.literal: Ze had martial awe; border people feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's presence on the frontier was fearsome, and the border peoples bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 渭曲之役，則為西師圍逼，棄城奔梁。

translations.literal: At the Weiqu campaign Ze was pressed by the Western army's siege, abandoned the city, and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At Weiqu the Western army hemmed him in; he abandoned his city and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁尋放還，神武恕而不責。

translations.literal: Liang soon released and returned him; Gao Huan pardoned and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang soon sent him back, and Gao Huan pardoned him without punishment.

sentences.zh: 元象初，洛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanxiang era he was made inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 以前後勳，封太原縣伯。

translations.literal: For former and later merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Taiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 則性貪，在州不法，舊京諸像，毀以鑄錢，于時號河陽錢，皆出其家。

translations.literal: Ze's nature was greedy; in the province he acted unlawfully, destroyed the old capital's statues to cast coin, and at the time the coins called Heyang money all came from his household.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was greedy; in office he broke the law, melted down the old capital's Buddhist images to cast cash—the so-called Heyang coins of the day all came from his house.

sentences.zh: 以武用，除徐州刺史，取受狼籍。

translations.literal: For martial utility he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province and took bribes in sprawling disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his military record he was made inspector of Xu Province, where his extortion knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 令送晉陽，文襄怒其罪。

translations.literal: He was ordered sent to Jinyang; Wenxiang was angry at his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered sent to Jinyang, and Gao Cheng was incensed at his offenses.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡烈懿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Works, posthumous name Fierce and Virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of works, with the posthumous name Fierce and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 則弟敬寶，位東廣州刺史，與蕭軌攻建業，不克，死焉。

translations.literal: Ze's younger brother Jingbao held the post of Inspector of Eastern Guang Province; with Xiao Gui he attacked Jianye, did not take it, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's younger brother Jingbao was inspector of Eastern Guang Province; he joined Xiao Gui in an assault on Jianye, failed to take the city, and died in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗，字紹宗，晃第四子太原王恪之後也。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong, style name Shaozong, was a descendant of Prince of Taiyuan Ke, fourth son of Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong, who used Shaozong as his style, was descended from Prince Ke of Taiyuan, fourth son of Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖騰，歸魏，遂居代。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Teng submitted to Wei and then dwelt in Dai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Teng submitted to Wei and settled in Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖郁，岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 父遠，恆州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had been inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 紹宗容貌恢毅，少言，深沉有膽略。

translations.literal: Shaozong's appearance was vast and resolute; he spoke little, was deep and possessed stratagem and daring.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong was broad-faced and stern, sparing of speech, deep-minded, and bold in counsel.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮即其從舅子也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong was precisely his mother's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was his cousin on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛，私告曰：「洛中人士繁盛，驕侈成俗，不除翦，恐難制。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, he privately told him: "The people of Luoyang are numerous and flourishing; arrogance and extravagance have become custom—if we do not cut them down, I fear they will be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang he took Shaozong aside and said, "Luoyang is crowded with men grown rich and proud—extravagance is the custom now. Unless we cut them down, I fear we cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 吾欲因百官出迎，悉誅之，若何？」

translations.literal: I wish to take advantage of the hundred officials coming out to welcome us and kill them all—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to use the officials' welcoming ceremony to slaughter them all—what do you say?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「太后淫虐，天下共棄。

translations.literal: He replied: "The empress dowager is licentious and cruel; the realm together casts her off.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong answered, "The empress dowager is vicious and debauched—the realm has turned from her.

sentences.zh: 公既執忠義，忽欲殲夷多士，實謂非策。」

translations.literal: Your Grace already holds righteousness and loyalty, yet suddenly wishes to annihilate the many scholars—this is truly called not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: You came as the champion of righteousness; to slaughter the court's men in a single stroke would be no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Rong would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功封索盧侯，遷爾硃兆長史。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Suolu and was transferred to Erzhu Zhao's chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as Marquis of Suolu for military merit and became chief clerk to Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及兆敗，紹宗于烏突城見神武，遂攜爾硃榮妻子並兆余眾自歸神武。

translations.literal: When Zhao was defeated, Shaozong at Wutu city met Gao Huan; he then carried Erzhu Rong's wife and children together with Zhao's remaining masses and of himself returned to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao fell, Shaozong met Gao Huan at Wutu, brought him Erzhu Rong's family, Zhao's remaining troops, and submitted in person.

sentences.zh: 神武仍加恩禮，所有官爵並如故，軍謀兵略，時參預焉。

translations.literal: Gao Huan still added favor and courtesy; all his offices and titles remained as before, and in army plans and military stratagems he was at times allowed to take part.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan treated him with added favor; his offices and titles were left unchanged, and he was often consulted on campaigns and strategy.

sentences.zh: 及遷鄴，令紹宗與高隆之共知府庫、圖籍諸事。

translations.literal: When they moved the capital to Ye, he ordered Shaozong and Gao Longzhi jointly to manage the treasury, maps and registers, and such affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the seat moved to Ye, he put Shaozong and Gao Longzhi jointly in charge of the treasury, archives, and related affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 時丞相記室孫搴屬紹宗，以其兄為州主簿，紹宗不用。

translations.literal: At the time the chancellor's staff officer Sun Qian entrusted Shaozong, asking that his elder brother be made the province's chief clerk; Shaozong did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's secretariat officer Sun Qian asked Shaozong to appoint his elder brother provincial chief clerk; Shaozong refused.

sentences.zh: 搴譖之神武曰：「紹宗嘗登廣固城長歎，謂所親云：大丈夫有復先業理不？」

translations.literal: Qian slandered him to Gao Huan, saying: "Shaozong once climbed Guanggu city and sighed long, telling those close to him: Does a great man have reason to restore his forefathers' enterprise?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian slandered him to Gao Huan, saying, "Shaozong once climbed the walls of Guanggu and sighed to his intimates, 'Is there not a way for a true man to restore his ancestors' realm?'

sentences.zh: 由是徵還。

translations.literal: Because of this he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: On that report he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 元象初，以軍功進爵為公，累遷御史中尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, for military merit his noble rank was advanced to duke; he was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanxiang era he was advanced to duke for military merit and rose to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 屬梁人劉烏黑入寇徐方，授徐州刺史。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang's man Liu Wuhei invaded Xu region; he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuhei of Liang raided the Xu region, he was appointed inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 執烏黑殺之。

translations.literal: He seized Wuhei and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Wuhei and executed him.

sentences.zh: 還，除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 侯景反，命紹宗為東南道行台，加開府，改封燕郡公，又與大都督高岳禽梁貞陽侯蕭明於寒山。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he ordered Shaozong to be Southeast Circuit Executive Agency, with added opening office, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Yancheng commandery, and again with Grand Chief Commander Gao Yue captured Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, at Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Shaozong was made executive of the southeast circuit, granted an opening office, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yancheng; he also joined Grand Chief Commander Gao Yue in capturing Xiao Ming, Marquis of Zhenyang of Liang, at Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 回軍討侯景于渦陽。

translations.literal: Turning the army, he campaigned against Hou Jing at Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned his army to campaign against Hou Jing at Guoyang.

sentences.zh: 時景軍甚盛，初聞韓軌往討之，曰：「啖豬腸小兒。」

translations.literal: At the time Jing's army was very strong; when he first heard Han Gui was going to campaign against him, he said: "That pig-gut-eating brat."
translations.idiomatic: Jing's forces were then at their height. When he first heard that Han Gui was coming against him, he sneered, "That pig-gut-eating whelp.

sentences.zh: 聞高嶽往，曰：「此兵精人凡爾。」

translations.literal: When he heard Gao Yue was going, he said: "These troops are sharp; the man is commonplace, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Gao Yue was sent, he said, "Sharp troops—but a commonplace commander."

sentences.zh: 諸將被輕。

translations.literal: The generals were treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The generals he dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 及聞紹宗至，扣鞍曰：「誰教鮮卑小兒解遣紹宗來？

translations.literal: When he heard Shaozong had arrived, he struck the saddle and said: "Who taught that Xianbei whelp to know how to send Shaozong?
translations.idiomatic: But when he learned Shaozong was coming, he slapped his saddle and cried, "Who taught that Xianbei pup to send Shaozong?

sentences.zh: 若然，高王未死邪？」

translations.literal: If so, is the Prince of Qi not dead after all?"
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, the Prince of Qi cannot be dead after all?

sentences.zh: 及與景戰，諸將頻敗，無肯先者。

translations.literal: When they battled with Jing, the generals were repeatedly defeated; none would go first.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, the other commanders were beaten again and again, and none would lead the charge.

sentences.zh: 紹宗麾兵徑進，諸將從之，因大捷。

translations.literal: Shaozong waved the troops straight forward; the generals followed him, and thereby there was a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong waved his men straight ahead; the others followed, and the day ended in a great victory.

sentences.zh: 西魏遣王思政據潁川，又以紹宗為南道行台，與太尉高岳、儀同劉豐圍擊之，堰洧水灌城。

translations.literal: Western Wei sent Wang Sizheng to hold Yingchuan; again they made Shaozong Southern Circuit Executive Agency; with Grand Commandant Gao Yue and Liu Feng with Pomp Equal Rank they besieged and struck him, damming the Xu River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei sent Wang Sizheng to hold Yingchuan, Shaozong was again made executive of the southern circuit; with Grand Commandant Gao Yue and Liu Feng, who held ceremonial parity, he besieged the city and dammed the Xu River to flood it.

sentences.zh: 時紹宗數有凶夢，每惡之，私謂左右曰：「吾自數年已還，恆有蒜發，昨來忽盡。

translations.literal: At that time Shaozong repeatedly had ominous dreams; each time he loathed them. Privately he told those about him, "For several years now I have constantly had garlic sprouts on my head; yesterday they suddenly all fell out.
translations.idiomatic: About then Shaozong had been troubled by repeated nightmares. He confided to his attendants, "For years I have kept sprouting garlic on my head—and yesterday it was suddenly all gone.

sentences.zh: 蒜者算也，其算盡乎！」

translations.literal: Garlic" [suan] is "calculation" [suan]; is my tally spent!"
translations.idiomatic: Garlic and "account" are the same word—have my days been counted out!

sentences.zh: 未幾，與劉豐臨堰，見北有塵氣，乃入艦同坐。

translations.literal: Before long, with Liu Feng he went to the dike; seeing dust to the north, they entered a ship and sat together.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he and Liu Feng were at the dam; when they saw dust rising to the north they boarded a ship and sat down together.

sentences.zh: 暴風從東北來，纜斷飄艦，徑向敵城。

translations.literal: A violent wind came from the northeast; the cables broke and the ship drifted, heading straight for the enemy city.
translations.idiomatic: A gale rose from the northeast, the mooring lines snapped, and the vessel drifted straight toward the enemy walls.

sentences.zh: 紹宗自度不免，遂投水卒。

translations.literal: Shaozong reckoned he could not escape and threw himself into the water, dying.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he could not survive, Shaozong threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 三軍將士，莫不悲惋，朝廷嗟傷焉。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of the three armies were all deeply grieved; the court lamented his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men throughout the army mourned him; the court grieved his death.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰景惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant, with the posthumous name Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 慕容士肅

translations.literal: Murong Shisu
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shisu

sentences.zh: 長子士肅，以謀反伏法。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shisu was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shisu was put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以紹宗功，罪止士肅身。

translations.literal: Because of Shaozong's merits, the court limited punishment to Shisu alone.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Shaozong's service, the court confined punishment to Shisu alone.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，配享文襄廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was given a share in sacrifices in the courtyard shrine of Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huangjian era he was granted a place in the shrine of Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 士肅弟三藏。

translations.literal: Shisu's younger brother Sanzang.
translations.idiomatic: Shisu's younger brother was Sanzang.

sentences.zh: 慕容三藏

translations.literal: Murong Sanzang
translations.idiomatic: Murong Sanzang

sentences.zh: 叱列平

translations.literal: Chi Lieping
translations.idiomatic: Chi Lieping

sentences.zh: 叱列平，字殺鬼，代郡西部人，世為酋帥。

translations.literal: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui, was a man of the western part of Dai commandery; for generations his house had been tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Lieping, styled Shagui, came from western Dai; his family had been tribal chiefs for generations.

sentences.zh: 平有容貌，美須髯，善射馭。

translations.literal: Ping had a handsome appearance, a fine beard, and was skilled at archery and charioteering.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome, wore a fine beard, and excelled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 襲第一領人酋長、臨江伯。

translations.literal: He inherited the post of chief of the first following of men and was made Baron of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited leadership of the first following and was made Baron of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 魏末，以軍功至武衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he rose through military merit to General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In late Wei he rose by military merit to General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 隨爾硃榮破葛榮，平元顥，封癭陶縣伯。

translations.literal: He followed Erzhu Rong in defeating Ge Rong and pacifying Yuan Hao, and was enfeoffed Baron of Yingtao county.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Erzhu Rong, he helped defeat Ge Rong and pacify Yuan Hao and was enfeoffed Baron of Yingtao.

sentences.zh: 榮死，爾硃氏陵僭。

translations.literal: When Rong died, the Erzhu clan grew arrogant and overstepped.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death the Erzhu clan grew insolent and usurped power.

sentences.zh: 平懼禍，後歸神武。

translations.literal: Ping feared calamity and later went over to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disaster, Ping later submitted to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 從破四胡于韓陵。

translations.literal: He followed in crushing the Four Hu at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in crushing the Four Hu at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 以軍功，天保初累遷袞州刺史，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: For military merit, at the beginning of Tianbao he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Yan Prefecture and made Palace Attendant with Pomp Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: For his deeds at the opening of Tianbao he rose to governor of Yan Province and was made a palace attendant with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都督、瀛州刺史，諡曰莊惠。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made area commander-in-chief and Governor of Ying Prefecture, posthumous name Zhuanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made area commander and governor of Ying Prefecture, with the posthumous name Zhuanghui.

sentences.zh: 子孝沖嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaochong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaochong inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 孝沖弟長叉，武平末，侍中、開府儀同三司，封新甯王。

translations.literal: Xiaochong's younger brother Changcha; at the end of Wuping he was Palace Attendant, Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed Prince of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochong's younger brother Changcha, in late Wuping, was made palace attendant with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed Prince of Xinning.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，位上柱國，卒于涇州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he held the rank of Senior Pillar of the State and died as Governor of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Kaihuang era he reached Senior Pillar of the State and died in office as governor of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長叉無他才技，在官以清幹稱。

translations.literal: Changcha had no other talent; in office he was known for integrity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Changcha had no special gifts beyond a reputation for clean, capable administration.

sentences.zh: 步大汗薩

translations.literal: Buda Hansa
translations.idiomatic: Buda Hansa

sentences.zh: 步大汗薩，代郡西部人。

translations.literal: Buda Hansa was a man of the western part of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Buda Hansa was from western Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖榮，代郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rong was Administrator of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rong had been administrator of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父居，龍驤將軍、領人別將。

translations.literal: His father Ju was General of the Dragon-Charger and a following leader at separate command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju had been General of the Dragon Charger and a tribal following chief.

sentences.zh: 薩初從爾硃榮入洛。

translations.literal: At first Hansa followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hansa first followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及平葛榮，累功為都督。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was pacified he accumulated merit and became area commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Ge Rong he rose by accumulated merit to area commander.

sentences.zh: 榮死，又從兆入洛。

translations.literal: When Rong died he again followed Zhao into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died he again followed Zhao into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之敗，以所部降神武。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Hanling he surrendered his command to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Hanling he surrendered his troops to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷車騎大將軍，封行唐縣公，晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Cavalry General, enfeoffed Duke of Xingtang county, and made Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Grand Cavalry General, enfeoffed Duke of Xingtang, and made governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，改封義陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Qi received the Mandate his fief was changed to Duke of Yiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his fief was changed to Duke of Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 薛脩義

translations.literal: Xue Xiuyi
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi

sentences.zh: 薛修義，字公讓，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiuyi, styled Gongrang, was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹，魏七兵尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shao was Wei Director of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao had been Wei Director of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 祖壽仁，秦州刺史、汾陰公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouren was Governor of Qin Prefecture and Duke of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouren was governor of Qin Prefecture and Duke of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 父寶集，定陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Baoji was Administrator of Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baoji was administrator of Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 修義少而奸俠，輕財重氣。

translations.literal: In youth Xiuyi was knavish and chivalrous, lightly valuing wealth and heavily valuing spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was a reckless knight-errant who scorned money and prized loyalty.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，天下兵起，特詔募能得三千人者，用為別將。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang, when warfare swept the realm, a special edict promised that whoever could recruit three thousand men would be made a separate commander.
translations.idiomatic: In late Zhenguang, as revolt spread, an edict promised separate command to anyone who could raise three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 脩義得七千餘人，假安北將軍、西道別將。

translations.literal: Xiuyi got more than seven thousand men and was made acting General Who Pacifies the North and separate commander of the western circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi raised more than seven thousand and was made acting General Who Pacifies the North and separate commander on the western route.

sentences.zh: 以軍功，拜龍門鎮將。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Fortress Commander of Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was appointed defender of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 後宗人鳳賢等作亂，圍鎮城，修義以天下紛擾，遂為逆，自號黃鉞大將軍。

translations.literal: Later clansmen Feng Xian and others rebelled and besieged the fortress; seeing the realm in turmoil, Xiuyi turned rebel, styling himself Great General of the Yellow Ax.
translations.idiomatic: When kinsman Feng Xian and others rose and besieged the town, Xiuyi, finding the empire in chaos, rebelled and styled himself Great General of the Yellow Halberd.

sentences.zh: 詔都督宗正珍孫討之，軍未至，修義慚悔，遣表乞一大將招慰，乃降。

translations.literal: The edict made area commander Zongzheng Zhensun attack him; before the army arrived Xiuyi felt shame and regret and sent a memorial begging for a senior general to summon and comfort him, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zongzheng Zhensun against him, but before the troops arrived Xiuyi repented and petitioned for a high commissioner to accept his surrender—which he then offered.

sentences.zh: 鳳賢等猶據險不降，修義與書，降之。

translations.literal: Feng Xian and the others still held the heights and would not yield; Xiuyi wrote them letters and brought them down.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xian still held the high ground and refused to submit; Xiuyi wrote to him and secured his surrender.

sentences.zh: 乃授鳳賢龍驤將軍，陽夏子，改封汾陰縣侯。

translations.literal: Feng Xian was then appointed General of the Dragon-Charger and made Viscount of Yangxia; Xiuyi's fief was changed to Marquis of Fenyin county.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xian was made General of the Dragon Charger and Viscount of Yangxia; Xiuyi's fief was changed to Marquis of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮以修義反覆，錄送晉陽，與高昂等並見拘防。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, because Xiuyi was changeable, had him escorted to Jinyang and detained together with Gao Ang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, deeming Xiuyi untrustworthy, sent him to Jinyang and held him with Gao Ang and others.

sentences.zh: 榮赴洛，並以自隨，置於駝牛署。

translations.literal: When Rong went to Luoyang they were all taken along and placed in the Camel-Ox Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong marched on Luoyang they were taken along and confined in the Camel-Ox Office.

sentences.zh: 榮死，魏孝莊以修義為弘農、河北、河東、正平四郡大都督。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei made Xiuyi area commander of the four circuits Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death Emperor Xiaozhuang made Xiuyi grand coordinator of Hongnong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 時神武為晉州刺史，見之，相待甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan was Governor of Jin Prefecture; on meeting Xiuyi he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was then governor of Jin Prefecture and treated Xiuyi with exceptional warmth when they met.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之捷，以修義行并州事。

translations.literal: After the victory at Hanling, Xiuyi was put in charge of Bingzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Hanling, Xiuyi was put in charge of Bingzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝入關，神武以修義為關右行台，自龍門濟河，招下西魏北華州刺史薛崇禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the Pass, Gao Huan made Xiuyi executive of the Guanxi circuit; crossing the Yellow River from Longmen he won over Xue Chongli, Western Wei's governor of Northern Hua.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled into the Pass, Gao Huan made Xiuyi his Guanxi executive; crossing from Longmen he won over Xue Chongli, Western Wei's governor of Northern Hua.

sentences.zh: 初，神武欲大城晉，中外府司馬房毓曰：「若使賊到此處，雖城何益？」

translations.literal: At first Gao Huan wished to wall Jin greatly; Fang Yu, master of records in the central and external offices, said: "If bandits reach this place, of what use is a wall?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan at first wanted to fortify Jin on a grand scale, but Fang Yu of the headquarters staff said, "If the enemy reaches this far, what good will walls do?

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 及沙苑之敗，徙秦、南汾、東雍三州人於并州，又欲棄晉，以遣家屬向英雄城。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shawei the people of Qin, Southern Fen, and Eastern Yong prefectures were moved into Bingzhou, and they again wished to abandon Jin and send families toward Yingxiong Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: After Shawei the populations of Qin, Southern Fen, and Eastern Yong were moved into Bingzhou; the court again considered abandoning Jin and sending families to Yingxiong Fortress.

sentences.zh: 修義諫曰：「若晉州敗，定州亦不可保。」

translations.literal: Xiuyi remonstrated: "If Jinzhou falls, Dingzhou cannot be preserved either."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi urged, "If Jin Prefecture falls, Ding Prefecture cannot be held either.

sentences.zh: 神武怒曰：「爾輩皆負我，前不聽我城并州城，使我無所趣。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan said angrily: "You lot have all failed me; before you would not heed me in walling Bingzhou's city, so I had nowhere to turn."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan flared up: "You have all betrayed me—because you would not fortify Bingzhou when I asked, I had nowhere left to go.

sentences.zh: 修義曰：「若失守，則請誅。」

translations.literal: Xiuyi said: "If I lose the defense, then request my execution."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi answered, "If the city falls, ask for my head.

sentences.zh: 斛律金曰：「還仰漢小兒守，收家口為質，勿與兵馬。」

translations.literal: Hulu Jin said: "Send the Northerners back to let the Han stripling hold it, gather their families as hostages, and give them no troops or horses."
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Jin said, "Let the northern soldiery hold it, take their families as hostages, and withhold troops and mounts.

sentences.zh: 神武從之，以修義行晉州事。

translations.literal: Gao Huan followed this and put Xiuyi in charge of Jinzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan agreed and left Xiuyi in charge of Jin.

sentences.zh: 及西魏儀同長孫子彥圍逼城下，修義開門伏甲侍之。

translations.literal: When Western Wei's Ceremonial Equal Changsun Ziyan pressed the city, Xiuyi opened the gate and set armed men in ambush to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsun Ziyan of Western Wei, holding ceremonial parity, besieged the walls, Xiuyi opened the gates and laid an ambush within.

sentences.zh: 子彥不測虛實，於是遁去。

translations.literal: Ziyan could not gauge truth and falsehood, and thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to read the situation, Ziyan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神武嘉之，就拜晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan praised him and at once appointed him Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan praised him and promptly appointed him governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 後除齊州刺史，以黷貨除名。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Qi Prefecture and removed from office for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Qi Prefecture, then stripped of rank for graft.

sentences.zh: 追其守晉州功，復其官爵。

translations.literal: In consideration of his merit defending Jinzhou his titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: His titles were restored in recognition of his defense of Jin.

sentences.zh: 俄以軍功，進正平郡公，加開府。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, for military merit, he was advanced to Duke of Zhengping commandery with an opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for further military merit, he was advanced to Duke of Zhengping commandery and given an opening office.

sentences.zh: 天保中，卒于太子太保，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he died as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he died as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子文殊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wenshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenshu inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 修義從弟嘉族，性亦豪爽。

translations.literal: Xiuyi's younger cousin Jiazu was likewise bold and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi's younger kinsman Jiazu was likewise open-handed and proud.

sentences.zh: 從神武平四胡于韓陵。

translations.literal: He followed Gao Huan in pacifying the Four Hu at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in the pacification of the Four Hu at Hanling.

sentences.zh: 歷華、陽二州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Hua and Yang prefectures in succession and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as governor of Hua and Yang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子震，字文雄，位廉州刺史，亦著軍功。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, styled Wenxiong, held the post of Governor of Lian Prefecture and likewise won military merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, styled Wenxiong, became governor of Lian Prefecture and likewise distinguished himself in war.

sentences.zh: 又歷南汾、譙二州刺史。

translations.literal: He also served as Governor of Southern Fen and Qiao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Southern Fen and Qiao as well.

sentences.zh: 慕容儼

translations.literal: Murong Yan
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan

sentences.zh: 慕容儼，字恃德，清都人，廆之後也。

translations.literal: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was of Qingdu; he was a descendant of Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yan, styled Shide, was from Qingdu, a descendant of Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 容貌出群，衣冠甚偉，不好讀書，頗學兵法。

translations.literal: His appearance stood above the crowd; his cap and robes were very grand; he did not love reading books but studied military methods quite a bit.
translations.idiomatic: His looks set him apart, and he dressed with imposing splendor; he cared little for books but studied the art of war.

sentences.zh: 爾硃氏敗，歸神武。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan fell he went over to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu fell he submitted to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 以勳，累遷五城太守。

translations.literal: Through merit he was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he rose to administrator of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 見東雍州刺史潘相樂，長揖而已。

translations.literal: On meeting Eastern Yong Prefecture Governor Pan Xiangyue he merely made a long bow.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Pan Xiangyue, governor of Eastern Yong, he offered only a long bow.

sentences.zh: 丞尉已下，數罹其罪。

translations.literal: Assistants and constables below suffered his punishments many times.
translations.idiomatic: His deputies and constables suffered punishment again and again.

sentences.zh: 乃謂儼曰：「府君，少為群下屈節。」

translations.literal: He thereupon said to Yan: "Governor, for the little while you must bow to the ranks below."
translations.idiomatic: Pan said to him, "For a time, my lord, you will have to bow to your subordinates.

sentences.zh: 儼攘袂曰：「吾狀貌如此，行望人拜，豈可拜人！」

translations.literal: Yan swept back his sleeve and said: "With this appearance of mine, where I walk I expect men to bow to me—how could I bow to others!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan swept back his sleeve and said, "With a body like mine, people bow when they see me coming—why should I bow to anyone?

sentences.zh: 神武聞二人在邊不和，征相樂還朝，以儼代為刺史。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan heard that the two men on the border were not in harmony, he summoned Xiangyue back to court and replaced him with Yan as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of their feud, Gao Huan recalled Xiangyue and replaced him with Yan.

sentences.zh: 遷東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Eastern Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Eastern Jing.

sentences.zh: 行次長社，忽為其部下人所執，將投山賊張儉，為守人王崇祖私放，獲免。

translations.literal: Passing Changshe, he was suddenly seized by men of his command who meant to hand him over to the mountain bandit Zhang Jian; the guard Wang Chongzu secretly released him and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshe his own troops seized him, meaning to deliver him to the bandit Zhang Jian; the watchman Wang Chongzu freed him in secret and he escaped death.

sentences.zh: 神武仍授以軍司，共擊平儉，始得達州。

translations.literal: Gao Huan then appointed him army supervisor; together they attacked and pacified Jian, and only then did he reach his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan made him army supervisor, and only after they jointly crushed Zhang Jian could he reach his post.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，時諸州多翻陷，唯儼獲全。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Shawei, most prefectures turned and fell; only Yan came through unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: After Shawei, when prefectures everywhere defected, Yan alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以軍功，除開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for military merit he was made Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies with an opening office.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was made a palace attendant with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies for his military merit.

sentences.zh: 六年，梁司徒陸法和、儀同宋茝等以郢州城內附。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Liang Minister of Works Lu Fahe and Ceremonial Equal Song Chi and others brought Ying Prefecture city over to submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Liang Minister of Works Lu Fahe, Ceremonial Equal Song Chi, and others surrendered Ying Prefecture to Qi.

sentences.zh: 時清河王岳帥師江上，議以城在江外，求忠勇過人者守之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qinghe Yue commanded troops on the Yangzi; they discussed that the city lay beyond the river and sought someone surpassing others in loyalty and courage to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Yue was then commanding on the Yangzi; the council said the city lay beyond the river and required a man of proven courage and loyalty to hold it.

sentences.zh: 眾推儼，遂遣鎮郢城。

translations.literal: The masses pushed Yan, and he was sent to garrison Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: All eyes turned to Yan, and he was sent to defend Ying.

sentences.zh: 始入而梁大都督侯瑱、任約率水陸軍奄至城下，於上流鸚鵡洲造荻葓，竟數里，以塞船路。

translations.literal: He had just entered when Liang Grand Area Commander Hou Jin and Ren Yue led water and land forces suddenly to the walls; upstream at Parrot Isle they built a reed matting barrier several li long to block the shipping lane.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely entered when Hou Jin and Ren Yue brought land and river forces against the walls; upstream at Parrot Isle they built a reed barrier miles long to choke the channel.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，儼悅以安之。

translations.literal: The masses were afraid; Yan delighted them to steady them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were afraid, but Yan put on a cheerful face and steadied them.

sentences.zh: 城中先有神祠一所，俗號城隍神，儼於是順士卒心祈請，須臾，沖風驚波，漂斷荻葓。

translations.literal: Within the city there was first a spirit shrine commonly called the City-God; Yan thereupon followed the soldiers' hearts in prayer; in an instant a rushing wind and startled waves floated away and broke the reed barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The city held a shrine popularly called the City God; Yan prayed there as the soldiers wished, and in a moment a gale rose and shattered the reed barrier.

sentences.zh: 約復以鐵鎖連緝，防禦彌切。

translations.literal: Yue again joined them with iron chains in continuous links; the defense grew all the stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue linked iron chains across the stream and tightened the blockade.

sentences.zh: 儼還，共祈請，風浪夜驚，葓復斷絕。

translations.literal: Yan returned; together they prayed; wind and waves startled the night; the reed barrier was broken apart again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan returned to the shrine and prayed with them; that night a gale shattered the reed barrier once more.

sentences.zh: 如此再三，城人大喜，以為神助。

translations.literal: Thus three times over; the people in the city were greatly pleased and took it for divine aid.
translations.idiomatic: After this happened again and again, the townspeople rejoiced, believing heaven itself was helping them.

sentences.zh: 儼出城奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Yan went out of the city and struck fiercely, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sallied forth and struck hard, routing the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 瑱、約又並力圍城。

translations.literal: Jin and Yue again joined forces to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jin and Ren Yue joined forces again and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 唯煮槐楮葉並糸寧根、水葒、葛、艾等及靴、皮帶、筋角等食之。

translations.literal: They boiled only locust and paper-mulberry leaves together with ning-root, water smartweed, kudzu, mugwort, and the like, and ate boots, leather belts, sinew, horn, and such.
translations.idiomatic: They had nothing to eat but boiled locust and mulberry leaves, wild roots, smartweed, kudzu, mugwort, and even boots, belts, sinew, and horn.

sentences.zh: 人死，即火別分食，唯留骸骨。

translations.literal: When a man died, they at once roasted him by fire, divided the flesh to eat, and kept only the bones.
translations.idiomatic: When someone died, they roasted the body, divided the flesh for food, and left only the bones.

sentences.zh: 儼猶信賞必罰，分甘同苦。

translations.literal: Yan still believed rewards and punishments were sure; he shared sweetness and shared bitterness alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yan still held fast to reward and punishment, sharing every hardship with his men.

sentences.zh: 自正月至六月，人無異志。

translations.literal: From the first month to the sixth month, among the people there was no change of will.
translations.idiomatic: From the first month through the sixth, not one man wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後蕭方智立，請和。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Fangzhi was established and sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xiao Fangzhi came to the throne, Liang sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 文宣以城在江表，有詔還之。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, because the city lay south of the Yangzi, issued an edict to bring Yan back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan, judging that the city lay deep in the south, ordered Yan brought home.

sentences.zh: 及至，望帝悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he saw the emperor and grief overcame him beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at court, he saw the emperor and was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 帝親執其手，捋儼須，脫帽看發，歎自久之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally took his hand, stroked Yan's beard, removed his cap to look at his hair, and sighed a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand, stroked Yan's beard, lifted his cap to look at his hair, and sighed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 曰：「自古忠烈，豈過此也！」

translations.literal: He said: "Loyal martyrs since antiquity—could any surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Loyal martyrs since antiquity—who could surpass this?"

sentences.zh: 除趙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 天統四年，別封寄氏縣公，並賜金銀酒鐘各一枚、胡馬一疋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiantong he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Jishi county, and was also granted one gold and one silver wine vessel each and one barbarian horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiantong he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Jishi, with a gold and a silver wine cup and a steppe horse.

sentences.zh: 五年，進爵為義安王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his rank was advanced to Prince of Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was raised to Prince of Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，為光州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he became Governor of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he became governor of Guang.

sentences.zh: 儼少從征討，經略雖非所長，而有將帥之節。

translations.literal: Yan from youth followed campaigns; though grand strategy was not his strength, he possessed a commander's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had campaigned since youth; strategy was not his gift, but he had the bearing of a true commander.

sentences.zh: 所曆諸州，雖不能清白守道，亦不貪殘害物。

translations.literal: In every prefecture he passed through, though he could not keep pure integrity and hold to the Way, he also was not greedy or cruel in harming things.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefectures he governed he was no model of spotless integrity, yet he was never rapacious or cruel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 子子會，位郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zihui held the post of Governor of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zihui served as governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平鄴，使其子送敕喻之，子會枷其子，付獄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Ye, he sent his son with an edict to instruct Zihui; Zihui put his son in the cangue and handed him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou took Ye, he sent his son with an edict to summon Zihui; Zihui clapped his own son in the stocks and threw him into prison.

sentences.zh: 尋赦書至，雲行台武王已降，子會乃與僚屬北面慟哭，然後奏命。

translations.literal: Soon a pardon arrived, saying the Prince of Wu at the Front Office had already surrendered; Zihui then with his staff faced north and wailed bitterly, and only afterward reported to receive orders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a pardon arrived saying the Prince of Wu at the Front Office had surrendered; Zihui and his staff turned north and wept bitterly, then submitted to the new order.

sentences.zh: 爾硃氏將帥歸神武者，又有代人厙狄伏連，字仲山，本名伏憐，語音連。

translations.literal: Among the Erzhu clan generals who went over to Gao Huan there was also the Dai man Shedi Fulian, styled Zhongshan; his original name was Fulian, but in speech it sounded like Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Erzhu generals who submitted to Gao Huan was the Dai tribesman Shedi Fulian, styled Zhongshan; his birth name was Fulian, which in speech sounded like Lian.

sentences.zh: 事爾硃榮至直閣將軍。

translations.literal: He served Erzhu Rong up to Direct-Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: He served Erzhu Rong until he became a Direct-Gate General.

sentences.zh: 後從神武，賜爵蛇丘男。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan and was granted the title Baron of Sheqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Sheqiu.

sentences.zh: 天保初，儀同三司，尋加開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies; soon an opening office was added.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was made a palace attendant with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies, and soon received an opening office.

sentences.zh: 性質樸，勤公事，直衛官闕，曉夕不離帝所，頗以此見知。

translations.literal: His nature was plain and simple; he was diligent in public business; when the direct guard post was vacant he did not leave the emperor's side from dawn to dusk, and for this was quite noticed and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and dutiful, he never left the emperor's side from dawn to dusk when the palace guard post fell vacant, and won considerable favor thereby.

sentences.zh: 然鄙吝愚狠。

translations.literal: Yet he was mean, stingy, foolish, and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was miserly, foolish, and brutal.

sentences.zh: 為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: He became Governor of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 好聚斂，又嚴酷，居室患蠅，杖門者曰：「何故聽入！」

translations.literal: He loved amassing wealth and was also harsh; flies troubled his dwelling, and he beat the doorkeeper, saying: "Why did you let them in!"
translations.idiomatic: He loved extortion and ruled with cruelty; when flies plagued his rooms he beat the doorkeeper, crying, "Why did you let them in?"

sentences.zh: 其妻病，以百錢買藥，每日恨之。

translations.literal: When his wife fell ill, she bought medicine for a hundred cash, and each day he resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife fell ill and spent a hundred cash on medicine, he nursed the grievance day after day.

sentences.zh: 不識士流。

translations.literal: He did not recognize the gentry stream.
translations.idiomatic: He had no regard for men of breeding.

sentences.zh: 開府參軍，多是衣冠士族，皆加捶撻，逼遣築牆。

translations.literal: Opening-office aides were mostly cap-and-gown clansmen; all were given beating and flogging and driven off to build walls.
translations.idiomatic: His opening-office aides were mostly gentry; he had them flogged and driven out to build walls.

sentences.zh: 武平中，封宜都郡王，除領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yidu commandery and made Grand General of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuping he was made Prince of Yidu and Grand General of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 尋與琅邪王矯殺和士開，伏誅，被支解。

translations.literal: Soon, with the Prince of Langya, he falsely killed He Shikai; he was executed and dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined the Prince of Langya in the plot that killed He Shikai; he was executed and torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 伏連家口百餘，盛夏，人料倉米二升，不給鹽菜，常有饑色。

translations.literal: Fulian's household numbered more than a hundred; in midsummer each person was rationed two sheng of granary grain, with no salt or vegetables supplied, and they often wore the look of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian's household of more than a hundred souls received two sheng of granary grain apiece in midsummer, with no salt or vegetables, and hunger was written on every face.

sentences.zh: 冬至日，親表稱賀，其妻為設豆餅。

translations.literal: On the winter solstice, kin and friends offered congratulations; his wife set out bean cakes for them.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice, when kin and friends came to congratulate him, his wife served bean cakes.

sentences.zh: 問豆餅得處，雲于馬豆中分減。

translations.literal: Asked where the bean cakes came from, she said they had been taken by reducing the horses' bean fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where the cakes came from, she said she had skimmed them from the horses' bean fodder.

sentences.zh: 伏連大怒，典馬、掌食人並加杖罰。

translations.literal: Fulian was greatly enraged; the horse steward and the food steward were both given beating punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Fulian flew into a rage and had both the horse steward and the commissary flogged.

sentences.zh: 積年賜物，藏在別庫，遣一婢專掌管龠。

translations.literal: Gifts accumulated over years were stored in a separate treasury; he sent one maid to manage the keys exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Years of imperial gifts he hoarded in a separate storehouse, with one maid holding the keys.

sentences.zh: 每入庫檢閱，必語妻子；

translations.literal: Each time he entered the storehouse to inspect, he always told wife and children:
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went in to inspect the storehouse he told his wife and children,

sentences.zh: 此官物，不得輒用。

translations.literal: these are official goods; you must not use them rashly.
translations.idiomatic: "These are state goods—do not touch them."

sentences.zh: 至死時，唯著敝衤3〗軍；

translations.literal: At the time of his death he wore only worn drawers;
translations.idiomatic: At his death he wore nothing but tattered drawers;

sentences.zh: 而積絹至二萬疋，簿錄並歸天府。

translations.literal: yet silk he had amassed reached twenty thousand bolts; the register and all were turned over to the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: yet he had hoarded twenty thousand bolts of silk, every roll entered in the ledgers and sent to the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 潘樂，字相貴，廣甯石門人也。

translations.literal: Pan Le, styled Xianggui, was a man of Shimen in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Le, styled Xianggui, was from Shimen in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 本廣宗大族，魏世分鎮北邊，因家焉。

translations.literal: Originally a great clan of Guangzong; in the Wei era they were posted to garrison the northern border and made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was originally a great house of Guangzong; in Wei times they were posted to the northern frontier and settled there.

sentences.zh: 父永，有技藝，襲爵廣宗男。

translations.literal: His father Yong had technical skill and inherited the title Baron of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong was skilled in the crafts and inherited the barony of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 樂初生，有一雀止其母左肩，占者咸言富貴之征，因名相貴，後始為字。

translations.literal: When Le was first born a sparrow alighted on his mother's left shoulder; diviners all said it was a sign of wealth and honor, and so he was named Xianggui, which later became his style.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth a sparrow settled on his mother's left shoulder; diviners called it a mark of wealth and rank, so he was named Xianggui, which later became his style.

sentences.zh: 及長，寬厚有膽略。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was generous and possessed courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he was magnanimous and bold.

sentences.zh: 初歸葛榮，榮授京兆王，時年十九。

translations.literal: At first he went over to Ge Rong; Rong made him Prince of Jingzhao when he was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: He first joined Ge Rong, who at nineteen made him Prince of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 榮敗，隨爾硃榮，為別將討元顥，以功封敷城縣男。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated he followed Erzhu Rong, served as separate general against Yuan Hao, and for merit was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng county.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's defeat he followed Erzhu Rong, campaigned against Yuan Hao as a separate commander, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 齊神武出牧晉州，引樂為鎮城都將。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu went out to pasture Jin Prefecture he brought Le in as Metropolitan Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan took up the governorship of Jin, he made Le metropolitan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 後從破爾硃兆于廣阿，進爵廣宗縣伯。

translations.literal: Later he followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was advanced to Earl of Guangzong county.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was raised to Earl of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 累以軍功，拜東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Repeatedly through military merit he was appointed Governor of Eastern Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated military merit he was made governor of Eastern Yong.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗議欲廢州，樂以東雍地帶山河，境連胡、蜀，形勝之會，不可棄也，遂如故。

translations.literal: Gao Huan once discussed abolishing the prefecture; Le said Eastern Yong's land embraces mountains and rivers, its borders join the Hu and Shu regions, and it is a strategic convergence— it cannot be abandoned, and so it remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan once proposed abolishing the prefecture; Le argued that Eastern Yong lay among mountains and rivers where the frontiers met the Hu and Shu lands—a strategic hinge that must not be abandoned—and the post was kept.

sentences.zh: 後從破周師于河陰，議欲追之，令追者在西，不願者東，唯樂與劉豐居西。

translations.literal: Later he followed in defeating the Zhou army at Heyin; they discussed pursuing them and ordered pursuers to the west and the unwilling to the east; only Le and Liu Feng stood on the west.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory over the Zhou forces at Heyin, when pursuit was debated, those willing to chase went west and the rest east—only Le and Liu Feng chose the west.

sentences.zh: 神武善之，以眾之不同而止。

translations.literal: Gao Huan approved this and, because the masses differed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan approved, but because the command was divided he called the pursuit off.

sentences.zh: 改封金門郡公。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jinmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jinmen.

sentences.zh: 子子晃嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zihuang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zihuang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 諸將子弟，率多驕縱，子晃沈密謹愨，以清靖自居。

translations.literal: The sons of generals for the most part were arrogant and unrestrained; Zihuang was deep, careful, and dutiful, taking purity and quiet as his stand.
translations.idiomatic: Most generals' sons were proud and dissolute; Zihuang was grave, careful, and upright, holding himself to quiet integrity.

sentences.zh: 尚公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married an imperial princess and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He married an imperial princess and was made Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武平末，為幽州道行台右僕射、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was Right Vice Director of the Youzhou Circuit Front Office and Governor of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was Right Vice Director on the Youzhou circuit staff and governor of You.

sentences.zh: 周師將入鄴，子晃率突騎數萬赴援。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army was about to enter Ye, Zihuang led several tens of thousands of shock cavalry to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhou troops bore down on Ye, Zihuang led tens of thousands of shock cavalry to the relief.

sentences.zh: 至博陵，知鄴城不守，詣冀州降周齊王軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Boling, he learned Ye could not be held and went to Ji Prefecture to surrender to the Zhou Prince of Qi's army.
translations.idiomatic: At Boling he learned Ye could not be saved and went to Ji to surrender to the army of the Zhou Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 授上開府，隋大業初卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Upper Opening Office; he died at the beginning of Daye in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an upper opening-office holder and died early in the Daye era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 彭樂，字興，安定人也。

translations.literal: Peng Le, styled Xing, was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Le, styled Xing, was from Anding.

sentences.zh: 驍勇善騎射。

translations.literal: He was fierce and brave and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in battle and a master of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初隨杜洛周賊，知其不立，降爾硃榮。

translations.literal: At first he followed the bandit Du Luozhou; knowing he would not endure, he surrendered to Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed the rebel Du Luozhou; seeing the cause would not last, he surrendered to Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 從破葛榮於滏口。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Ge Rong at the Fu crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Ge Rong at the Fu crossing.

sentences.zh: 又為都督，從神武與行台僕射於暉討破羊侃於瑕丘。

translations.literal: Again as area commander he followed Gao Huan with Front Office Vice Director Yu Hui to defeat Yang Kan at Xiaqiu.
translations.idiomatic: As area commander he followed Gao Huan and Front Office Vice Director Yu Hui to defeat Yang Kan at Xiaqiu.

sentences.zh: 後叛投逆賊韓樓，封北平王。

translations.literal: Later he rebelled and went over to the traitor Han Lou, who enfeoffed him Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He later defected to the rebel Han Lou and was made Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮遣大都督侯深擊樓，樂又叛樓降深。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong sent Grand Area Commander Hou Shen to strike Lou, Le again rebelled against Lou and surrendered to Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong sent Grand Area Commander Hou Shen against Han Lou, Le defected again and surrendered to Hou Shen.

sentences.zh: 神武出山東，樂又隨從。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan came out to Shandong, Le again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched into Shandong, Le followed once more.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之役，樂先登陷陣，賊眾大崩，封樂城縣公。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling, Le was first to ascend and break the line; the rebel masses collapsed utterly; he was enfeoffed Duke of Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling he was first over the wall; the enemy ranks shattered, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，進爵汨陽郡公，除肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Later for military merit his rank was advanced to Duke of Miyang commandery and he was made Governor of Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For further merit he was raised to Duke of Miyang and made governor of Si.

sentences.zh: 天平四年，從神武西討，與周文相拒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he followed Gao Huan on the western campaign and faced Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianping he followed Gao Huan west and faced Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 神武欲緩持之，樂氣奮請決戰，曰：「我眾賊少，百人取一，差不可失也。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan wished to hold back and wear them down; Le's spirit flared and he begged for decisive battle, saying: "Our masses are many and the bandits few—take one in a hundred and the chance must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wanted to wear the enemy down, but Le burned to fight and begged for a decisive battle: "We outnumber them—pick one man in a hundred and we cannot miss this chance."

sentences.zh: 神武從之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan agreed.

sentences.zh: 樂因醉入深，被刺腸出，內之不盡，截去復戰，身被數創，軍勢遂挫，不利而還。

translations.literal: Le, because he was drunk, went in deep; he was stabbed and his intestines came out; he could not put them all back in, cut off the remainder, and fought again; his body received many wounds; the army's momentum was thus broken and they returned without advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Le charged too deep; stabbed, he could not tuck his bowels back in, cut off the hanging part, and fought on until he was covered in wounds; the army's momentum broke and they retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 神武每追諭以戒之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan often brought it up afterward to admonish and warn him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan often brought the episode up to warn him.

sentences.zh: 高仲密之叛也，周文援之，神武迎擊於芒山。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Yuwen Tai came to his aid; Gao Huan went to meet the blow at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Yuwen Tai marched to his aid and Gao Huan met him at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 候騎言賊去洛州四十里，蓐食乾飯，神武曰：「自應渴死，保待我殺！」

translations.literal: Scouts said the bandits were forty li from Lu Prefecture, eating dry rations on their rush mats; Gao Huan said: "They should die of thirst on their own—why wait for me to kill them!"
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported the enemy forty li from Lu, eating dry rations on the march; Gao Huan said, "They will die of thirst on their own—why should I bother to kill them?"

sentences.zh: 乃勒陣以待之。

translations.literal: He then drew up his ranks to wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up his ranks and waited.

sentences.zh: 西軍至皆喉氇參。

translations.literal: When the Western army arrived, all were on felt mats with dry provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western army came up, they were still eating dry fare on their felt mats.

sentences.zh: 樂以數千精騎為右甄，沖西軍北垂，所向奔退，遂馳入周文營。

translations.literal: Le with several thousand picked cavalry formed the right wing, struck the northern flank of the Western army, routed all before him, and galloped into Yuwen Tai's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Le led several thousand elite horsemen on the right, shattered the northern flank of the Western army, and galloped straight into Yuwen Tai's camp.

sentences.zh: 人告樂叛，神武曰：「樂棄韓樓事爾硃榮，背爾硃歸我，又叛入西。

translations.literal: Men reported that Le had rebelled; Gao Huan said: "Le abandoned Han Lou to serve Erzhu Rong, turned his back on the Erzhu to come to me, and again rebelled to enter the West.
translations.idiomatic: Someone cried that Le had turned traitor; Gao Huan said, "Le left Han Lou for Erzhu Rong, abandoned the Erzhu for me, and might betray me for the West.

sentences.zh: 事成敗豈在一樂？

translations.literal: Can success or failure hang on one Le alone?
translations.idiomatic: Does victory or defeat hang on Peng Le alone?

sentences.zh: 但念小人反覆爾。」

translations.literal: I only bear in mind that petty men are fickle, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I only remember how fickle such men can be."

sentences.zh: 俄而西北塵起，樂使告捷，虜西魏臨洮王東、蜀郡王榮宗、江夏王升、钜鹿王闡、譙郡王亮、詹事趙善，督將僚佐四十八人，皆系頸反接手，臨以刃，曆兩陣而唱名焉。

translations.literal: Soon dust rose in the northwest; Le's messenger reported victory, having captured Western Wei's Prince of Lintao, Dong; Prince of Shujun, Rongzong; Prince of Jiangxia, Sheng; Prince of Julu, Chan; Prince of Qiao, Liang; Grand Tutor Zhao Shan; and forty-eight commanders, officers, and staff—all with necks bound and hands reversed behind them, blades at their throats, paraded between the two armies while their names were called out.
