translations.idiomatic: Soon dust rose in the northwest; Le's messenger brought word of victory—Prince Dong of Lintao, Prince Rongzong of Shujun, Prince Sheng of Jiangxia, Prince Chan of Julu, Prince Liang of Qiao, Grand Tutor Zhao Shan, and forty-eight officers and staff, necks roped and hands bound behind them, blades at their throats, marched between the armies while their names were shouted aloud.

sentences.zh: 諸將乘勝，斬首三萬餘。

translations.literal: The generals pressed the victory and took more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pressed the victory and took more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 西軍退，神武使樂追之。

translations.literal: The Western army withdrew; Gao Huan sent Le to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: As the Western army fell back, Gao Huan sent Le in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 周文大窘而走，曰：「癡男子！

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai, hard pressed, fled and said: "Fool of a man!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai fled in distress and shouted, "You fool!

sentences.zh: 今日無我，明日豈有汝邪？

translations.literal: Today without me, tomorrow how could there be you?
translations.idiomatic: If I am gone today, will there be a tomorrow for you?

sentences.zh: 何不急還前營收金寶？」

translations.literal: Why not hurry back to the forward camp and gather gold and jewels?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not hurry back to the forward camp and loot the gold and jewels?"

sentences.zh: 樂從其言，獲周文金帶一束以歸，言周文漏刃破膽矣。

translations.literal: Le followed his words, took a bundle of Yuwen Tai's gold belt and returned, saying Yuwen Tai had slipped the blade and his courage was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Le took the bait, seized a bundle of Yuwen Tai's gold belt, and returned boasting that Yuwen Tai had slipped through his blade with his courage broken.

sentences.zh: 神武詰之，樂以周文言對。

translations.literal: Gao Huan questioned him; Le answered with Yuwen Tai's words.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan questioned him, and Le repeated Yuwen Tai's words.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「不為此語放之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Had it not been for those words I would not have let him go."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If not for that speech I would not have let him go."

sentences.zh: 神武雖喜其勝，且怒，令伏諸地，親稱其頭，連頓之，並數沙苑之失，舉刀將下者三，噤齘良久，乃止。

translations.literal: Gao Huan, though pleased at the victory, was also angry; he had Le lie on the ground, personally pressed his head down, and knocked it again and again, also reckoning up the defeat at Shayuan; thrice he raised the blade to strike and gnashed his teeth a long while before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was glad of the victory yet furious Le had let Tai escape; he had Le lie down, seized his head, and knocked it against the ground again and again, counting the defeat at Shayuan; thrice he raised the blade to strike, gnashed his teeth a long while, and at last stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 更請五千騎取周文。

translations.literal: Le again requested five thousand cavalry to take Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Le then asked for five thousand horse to capture Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 神武曰：「爾何放而復言捉邪？」

translations.literal: Gao Huan said: "Why did you let him go and again speak of capturing him?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Why did you let him go—and now speak of capturing him again?"

sentences.zh: 取絹三千疋壓樂，因賜之。

translations.literal: He took three thousand bolts of silk and pressed them on Le, then bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: He had three thousand bolts of silk heaped on Le and then gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷司徒。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he reached Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封陳留王，遷太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu and promoted to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was made Prince of Chenliu and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 二年，謀反，為前行襄州事劉章等告，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the second year he plotted rebellion; Liu Zhang and others in charge of forward affairs at Xiang Prefecture reported him, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he plotted rebellion; Liu Zhang and others handling forward affairs at Xiang reported him, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 暴顯，字思祖，魏郡斥丘人也。

translations.literal: Bao Xian, styled Sizu, was a man of Chiqiu in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xian, styled Sizu, came from Chiqiu in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖喟，仕魏，為朔州刺史，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kai served Wei as governor of Shuo Prefecture and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kai served Wei as governor of Shuo and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 父誕，恆州刺史、樂安公。

translations.literal: His father Dan was governor of Heng Prefecture and Duke of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan was governor of Heng and Duke of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 顯幼時，見一沙門指之曰：「此郎子好相表，大必為良將，貴極人臣。」

translations.literal: When Xian was young he saw a monk point at him and say: "This lad has an excellent physiognomy; grown he will surely be a fine general, noble to the utmost as a minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was young a monk pointed at him and said, "This boy has a noble face; grown he will surely be a fine general, exalted to the utmost among ministers."

sentences.zh: 語終失之。

translations.literal: When the speech ended he was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the words ended the monk was gone.

sentences.zh: 顯善騎射，曾從魏孝莊獵，一日中，手獲禽獸七十三。

translations.literal: Xian was skilled in mounted archery; he once followed Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei on a hunt and in a single day took seventy-three birds and beasts with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was skilled in mounted archery. He once followed Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei on a hunt and in one day took seventy-three birds and beasts with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 後從齊神武起義信都，累遷北徐州刺史，封屯留公。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army at Xindu, was repeatedly promoted to governor of Northern Xu, and enfeoffed Duke of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising the righteous army at Xindu, rose to governor of Northern Xu, and was enfeoffed Duke of Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 天保中，以贓貨解州，大理禁止。

translations.literal: During Tianbao, for taking bribes he was removed from his prefecture and confined by the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he was removed from office for bribery and confined by the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 處判未訖，為合肥被圍，遣顯與步大汗薩等攻梁北徐州，禽其刺史王強。

translations.literal: Before the sentence was finished, Hefei was besieged; they sent Xian with Buda Hansa and others to attack Liang's Northern Xu and captured its governor Wang Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before judgment was finished Hefei was besieged; Xian was sent with Buda Hansa and others to attack Liang's Northern Xu and capture its governor Wang Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天統中，累遷，位特進，封定陽王，卒。

translations.literal: During Tiantong he was repeatedly promoted, reached Special Advancement, was enfeoffed Prince of Dingyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiantong he rose through repeated promotions to Special Advancement, was enfeoffed Prince of Dingyang, and died.

sentences.zh: 皮景和

translations.literal: Pi Jinghe
translations.idiomatic: Pi Jinghe

sentences.zh: 皮景和，琅邪下邳人也。

translations.literal: Pi Jinghe was a man of Xiapi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Jinghe came from Xiapi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 父慶賓，魏淮南王開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Qingbin was a junior military aide in the opening office of the Prince of Huainan of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingbin was a junior military aide in the Prince of Huainan of Wei's opening office.

sentences.zh: 正光中，因使遇亂，遂家廣甯之石門縣。

translations.literal: During Zhenguang, while on a mission he encountered disorder and settled his family in Shimen county in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguang, on a mission he met the age's disorder and settled his family in Shimen county, Guangning.

sentences.zh: 景和少通敏，善騎射。

translations.literal: Jinghe in youth was quick and perceptive, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jinghe was quick and perceptive and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初以親信事神武。

translations.literal: At first he served Gao Huan as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served Gao Huan as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 後征步落稽，疑賊有伏，令景和將五六騎深入一穀。

translations.literal: Later when campaigning against the Buluoji, suspecting an ambush, [Gao Huan] ordered Jinghe to lead five or six horsemen deep into a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against the Buluoji, suspecting an ambush, he ordered Jinghe to take five or six horsemen deep into a ravine.

sentences.zh: 遇賊百餘人，便戰。

translations.literal: They met more than a hundred bandits and at once fought.
translations.idiomatic: They met more than a hundred bandits and fought at once.

sentences.zh: 景和射數十人，莫不應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Jinghe shot down scores of men; none failed to fall at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe shot down scores of men; every arrow dropped its man.

sentences.zh: 神武嘗令景和射一野豕，一箭獲之，深見賞異。

translations.literal: Gao Huan once had Jinghe shoot a wild boar; with one arrow he brought it down and was deeply regarded with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan once had Jinghe shoot a wild boar; one arrow brought it down, and he won deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 除庫直正都督。

translations.literal: He was made Regular Director of the Treasury Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular director of the treasury guards.

sentences.zh: 天保初，授通州刺史，封永寧縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed governor of Tong Prefecture and enfeoffed Viscount of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made governor of Tong and enfeoffed Viscount of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 景和趫捷，有武用，從襲庫莫奚，度黃龍，征契丹，定稽胡，討蠕蠕，每有戰功。

translations.literal: Jinghe was swift and agile with martial utility; he followed raids on the Kumo Xi, crossed Huanglong, campaigned against the Khitan, pacified the Jiehu, and attacked the Rouran—at every turn there was military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Swift and martial, Jinghe joined raids on the Kumo Xi, crossed Huanglong, fought the Khitan, pacified the Jiehu, and attacked the Rouran—winning merit at every turn.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中尚書、侍中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the palace secretariat and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 景和於武職中兼長吏事，又懷識平均，故頻有美授。

translations.literal: Among military posts Jinghe also excelled at civil administrative affairs; because he bore fair-minded discernment he frequently received fine appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Though a fighting man, he also handled civil affairs well; fair-minded and even-handed, he won repeated fine appointments.

sentences.zh: 周通好後，冠蓋往來，常令景和對接。

translations.literal: After Zhou and Qi made peace, envoys came and went in constant streams; he was regularly ordered to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou and Qi made peace, envoys came and went constantly, and he was regularly ordered to receive them.

sentences.zh: 每與同射，百發百中，甚見推重。

translations.literal: Whenever he shot alongside them it was a hundred hits in a hundred shots; he was greatly esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting with them he never missed; he was greatly esteemed.

sentences.zh: 武平中，詔獄多令中黃門等監之，恆令景和案覆，據理執正，由是過無枉濫。

translations.literal: During Wuping, imperial prison cases were often placed under supervision of palace eunuchs and such; Jinghe was constantly ordered to review files, holding to principle and insisting on what was right, and thereby excesses were not wrongly extensive.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuping, imperial prison cases were often supervised by palace eunuchs; Jinghe was constantly ordered to review them, hold to principle, and insist on justice—so that no case was wrongly pushed too far.

sentences.zh: 後除特進，封廣漢郡公，遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Special Advancement, enfeoffed Duke of Guanghan commandery, and transferred to General of the Palace Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Special Advancement, enfeoffed Duke of Guanghan, and made general of the palace garrison.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王之殺和士開，兵指西闕，內外莫知所為。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Langye killed He Shikai, troops pointed at the western gate tower; inside and outside none knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Langye killed He Shikai, troops massed at the western gate; court and city alike were at a loss.

sentences.zh: 景和請後主出千秋門，自號令。

translations.literal: Jinghe asked the Later Lord to go out through the Gate of a Thousand Autumns and issued commands himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe asked the Later Lord to go out through the Gate of a Thousand Autumns and took command himself.

sentences.zh: 事平，除尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed he was made right vice director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳將吳明徹寇淮南，令景和拒之。

translations.literal: Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan; [the court] ordered Jinghe to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Jinghe was ordered to resist him.

sentences.zh: 除領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was made Grand General of the Palace Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of the palace garrison.

sentences.zh: 封文城郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Prince of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Prince of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 又有平陽人鄭子饒，詐依佛道設齋會，用米麵不多，供贍甚廣，密從地藏，漸出餅飯。

translations.literal: There was also Zheng Zirao of Pingyang, who falsely relied on Buddhism to hold vegetarian feasts—using little rice and flour yet provisioning very generously, secretly from underground storage gradually producing cakes and rice.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zheng Zirao of Pingyang, who posed as a Buddhist, held feasts with little rice and flour yet fed a great crowd, and secretly from underground stores kept producing cakes and rice.

sentences.zh: 愚人以為神力，見信于魏、衛之間。

translations.literal: Foolish people took it for divine power; he was trusted between Wei and Wey.
translations.idiomatic: Fools took it for divine power, and he won believers between Wei and Wey.

sentences.zh: 將為逆亂，謀泄。

translations.literal: He was about to stage rebellion and the plot leaked.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to rebel; the plot leaked.

sentences.zh: 乃潛度河聚眾，自號長樂王，已破乘氏縣。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river in secret to gather followers, styled himself King of Changle, and had already taken Chengxian county.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river in secret, gathered followers, styled himself King of Changle, and had already seized Chengxian county.

sentences.zh: 景和遣騎擊破之，禽子饒，送鄴烹之。

translations.literal: Jinghe sent cavalry to crush him, captured Zirao, and sent him to Ye to be boiled alive.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe sent cavalry, broke him, captured Zirao, and sent him to Ye to be boiled alive.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹圍壽陽，敕景和與賀拔伏恩救之。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche besieged Shouyang, an edict ordered Jinghe and Heba Fu'en to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche besieged Shouyang, an edict ordered Jinghe and Heba Fu'en to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 是時，拒明徹者多傾覆，唯景和全軍而還。

translations.literal: At that time many who resisted Mingche met ruin; only Jinghe brought the army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Many who faced Mingche were ruined; only Jinghe brought his army back whole.

sentences.zh: 除尚書令。

translations.literal: He was made Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 武平六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wuping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuping he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉、錄尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as grand commandant and recorder of the department of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 長子信，機悟有風神。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xin was quick-witted with spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xin was quick-witted, with spirit and bearing.

sentences.zh: 位開府儀同三司、武衛將軍，于勳貴子弟中，稱其識鑒。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Military Guard General; among decorated noble sons he was praised for his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He held opening office, rank equal to the three excellencies, and military guard general; among sons of meritorious houses he was praised for discernment.

sentences.zh: 降周軍，授上開府、軍正中大夫。

translations.literal: He surrendered to the Zhou army and was appointed Upper Opening Office and Chief Rectifier of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered to the Zhou army and was made upper opening office and chief rectifier of the army.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒于洮州刺史。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang of Sui he died while serving as governor of Tao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang of Sui he died as governor of Tao.

sentences.zh: 少子宿達，開皇中，通事舍人。

translations.literal: The younger son Sudaa, during Kaihuang, was Master of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Sudaa, in Kaihuang, was master of communications.

sentences.zh: 母憂起復，將赴京，辭靈，慟哭而絕。

translations.literal: Rising from mourning before the mourning period ended, as he was about to go to the capital he took leave at the spirit tablet and wept until he lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning before the mourning term ended, as he was about to go to the capital he took leave at the spirit tablet and wept until he lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 久而獲蘇，不能下食，三日而死。

translations.literal: After a long while he revived but could not swallow food and died on the third day.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he revived but could not eat; on the third day he died.

sentences.zh: 綦連猛

translations.literal: Qi Lianmeng
translations.idiomatic: Qi Lianmeng

sentences.zh: 綦連猛，字武兒，代人也。

translations.literal: Qi Lianmeng, styled Wu'er, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Lianmeng, styled Wu'er, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先姬姓，六國末，避亂出塞，保祈連山，因以山為姓。

translations.literal: His ancestors were of the Ji clan; at the end of the Six States they fled disorder beyond the frontier passes, took refuge on Mount Qilian, and took the mountain as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were Ji clansmen; at the end of the Six States they fled turmoil beyond the passes, sheltered on Mount Qilian, and took the mountain as surname.

sentences.zh: 北人語訛，故曰綦連。

translations.literal: Northern speech slurred it, hence they are called Qilian.
translations.idiomatic: Northern speech slurred it, hence Qilian.

sentences.zh: 父元成，燕郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuancheng was governor of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuancheng was governor of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 猛少有志氣，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Meng in youth had spirit and resolve, adept with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Meng had spirit and resolve and was adept with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 初為爾硃榮親信。

translations.literal: At first he was a trusted intimate of Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Erzhu Rong's trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 榮被害，從爾硃兆入洛。

translations.literal: When Rong was killed he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was killed he followed Erzhu Zhao into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 猛父母兄弟皆在山東，爾硃京纏欲投神武，召之與俱。

translations.literal: Meng's parents, brothers, and kin were all in Shandong; Erzhu Jingchan wished to go over to Gao Huan and summoned Meng to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's parents, brothers, and kin were all in Shandong; Erzhu Jingchan wished to join Gao Huan and summoned Meng to go with him.

sentences.zh: 舉槊謂曰：「不從我者死！」

translations.literal: Raising his spear he said: "Whoever does not follow me dies!"
translations.idiomatic: Raising his spear he said, "Whoever does not follow me dies!"

sentences.zh: 乃從之。

translations.literal: So [Meng] followed him.
translations.idiomatic: So Meng followed.

sentences.zh: 去城五十餘里，猛以素蒙兆恩，即背京纏復歸兆。

translations.literal: Fifty-odd li from the city, Meng—having long received Zhao's favor—turned his back on Jingchan and returned again to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-odd li from the city, Meng—long favored by Zhao—turned on Jingchan and went back to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 兆敗，猛與斛律羌舉、乞伏貴和逃亡。

translations.literal: When Zhao was defeated, Meng fled with Hulu Qiangju and Qifu Guihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated, Meng fled with Hulu Qiangju and Qifu Guihe.

sentences.zh: 及見獲，各杖一百。

translations.literal: When they were captured, each was thrashed a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When they were captured, each was beaten a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 以猛配尉景，貴和配婁昭。

translations.literal: Meng was assigned to Wei Jing, Guihe to Lou Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was assigned to Wei Jing, Guihe to Lou Zhao.

sentences.zh: 羌舉以故酋長子，故無所配。

translations.literal: Qiangju, as son of a former tribal chief, therefore had no assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Qiangju, as son of a former tribal chief, had no assignment.

sentences.zh: 既而三人並為神武親信。

translations.literal: Before long all three again became trusted intimates of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long all three were again Gao Huan's trusted intimates.

sentences.zh: 後都督爾硃文暢將為逆，猛曰：「昔事其父兄，寧今日受死，不忍告而殺之。」

translations.literal: Later Area Commander Erzhu Wenchang was about to rebel; Meng said: "In the past I served his father and elder brothers; I would rather die today than inform on him and have him killed."
translations.idiomatic: Later area commander Erzhu Wenchang was about to rebel; Meng said, "I served his father and brothers; I would rather die today than betray him to have him killed."

sentences.zh: 神武聞之曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan heard it and said: "Serving a lord should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan heard it and said, "Loyalty should be like this."

sentences.zh: 舍其罪而益親之。

translations.literal: He pardoned his offense and drew him even closer.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned the offense and drew him closer still.

sentences.zh: 以軍功，封廣興縣侯。

translations.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guangxing county.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 梁使來聘，雲求角武藝。

translations.literal: A Liang envoy came on a mission, saying they wished to match martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: A Liang envoy came, asking to test martial skill.

sentences.zh: 文襄遣猛就館接之，雙帶兩鞬，左右馳射。

translations.literal: Wenxiang sent Meng to the guest lodge to receive them, wearing two quivers double-belted, riding left and right while shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Meng to the guest lodge to receive them, two quivers at his belt, shooting left and right at the gallop.

sentences.zh: 校挽強弓，梁人引弓兩張，皆三石；

translations.literal: They tested drawing strong bows; the Liang men drew two bows apiece, all of three piculs' pull;
translations.idiomatic: They tested the bow; the Liang men drew two bows apiece, each three piculs—

sentences.zh: 猛遂並取四張，疊挽之，過度。

translations.literal: Meng then took all four at once, drew them stacked, and exceeded their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Meng took all four, drew them stacked, and passed the mark.

sentences.zh: 梁人嗟服。

translations.literal: The men of Liang sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang envoys sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made governor of Eastern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made governor of Eastern Qin.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，加開府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing he was given Opening Office status.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he received opening office.

sentences.zh: 突厥侵逼晉陽，敕猛覘賊。

translations.literal: The Turks pressed and threatened Jinyang; an edict ordered Meng to reconnoiter the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks pressed Jinyang, an edict ordered Meng to scout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 中一騎將超出來鬥，猛即斬之。

translations.literal: One mounted officer among them charged out to duel; Meng at once cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: One enemy rider charged out to fight; Meng cut him down at once.

sentences.zh: 天統五年，除並省尚書令、領軍大將軍，封山陽王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs for the parallel provinces, Grand General of the Palace Garrison, and enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiantong he was made director of the department of state affairs for the parallel provinces and grand general of the palace garrison, and enfeoffed Prince of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 猛自和士開死後，漸預朝政，疑議與奪，咸亦咨稟。

translations.literal: From He Shikai's death onward Meng gradually took part in court government; doubtful points in counsel and decision were all also submitted to him for report.
translations.idiomatic: After He Shikai's death Meng gradually joined court deliberations; doubtful judgments and appointments were all referred to him.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深以猛武將之中，頗疾奸佞，言議時有可采，故引知機事。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen, among military men, noted that Meng greatly detested the treacherous and fawning; his opinions sometimes had what could be adopted—hence he was brought in to know critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen saw that among generals Meng especially hated treachery and flattery and that his counsel was sometimes worth taking, and drew him into confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖珽奏言猛與彥深前推琅邪王，事有意故。

translations.literal: Zu Ting memorialized that Meng and Yanshen had earlier promoted the Prince of Langye, the affair having deliberate cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting memorialized that Meng and Yanshen had earlier backed the Prince of Langye with deliberate intent.

sentences.zh: 於是出猛為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Meng was sent out as governor of Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was sent out as governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 彥深為西兗州刺史，即日首途。

translations.literal: Yanshen was made governor of Western Yan and set out the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen was made governor of Western Yan and set out the same day.

sentences.zh: 先是，謠曰：「七月刈禾太早，九月啖糕未好，本欲尋山射虎，激箭旁中趙老。」

translations.literal: Earlier a rhyme had said: "Harvesting grain in the seventh month is too soon; eating cakes in the ninth is not yet ripe; I meant to seek the mountain to shoot a tiger, but a stray arrow hit Old Zhao at the side."
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme had run: "Reaping in the seventh month is too soon; cakes in the ninth are not ready; I meant to hunt the mountain tiger, but a stray arrow struck Old Zhao."

sentences.zh: 至是，其言乃驗。

translations.literal: Now the words proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rhyme came true.

sentences.zh: 猛行至牛蘭，有人告和士開被害時，猛亦知情，遂被追還，削王爵，以開府赴州。

translations.literal: When Meng reached Niulan someone reported that at the time He Shikai was killed Meng too had knowledge; he was recalled, stripped of princely rank, and went to his post with Opening Office status only.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng reached Niulan someone reported he had known of He Shikai's murder; he was recalled, stripped of his princedom, and went to his post with opening office only.

sentences.zh: 在任寬惠清慎，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: In his post he was lenient, kind, and pure in caution; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was lenient, kind, and scrupulous; officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 淮陰王阿那肱與猛有舊，每欲攜引之，韓長鸞等沮難。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyin Anakhu was old friends with Meng and often wished to pull him along; Han Changluan and others obstructed and made it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyin Anakhu was old friends with Meng and often wished to advance him; Han Changluan and others blocked the way.

sentences.zh: 復授膠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again appointed governor of Jiao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made governor of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 後除大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，卒。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he entered Zhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 初，猛與尉興慶、謝猥餒並善射小心，給事神武左右。

translations.literal: Earlier Meng together with Wei Xingqing and Xie Wei'nei were all skilled at archery and careful in small matters, attending on Gao Huan's left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Meng, together with Wei Xingqing and Xie Wei'nei, were all skilled archers and careful attendants in Gao Huan's service.

sentences.zh: 神武使相者視之，曰：「猛大貴，尉、謝無官。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan had a physiognomist examine them and said: "Meng will be greatly honored; Wei and Xie will have no office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had a physiognomist examine them. "Meng will rise very high," he said; "Wei and Xie will never hold office.

sentences.zh: 及芒山之役，興慶救神武之窘，為軍所殺。

translations.literal: When the battle at Mount Mang came, Xingqing rescued Gao Huan from distress and was killed by the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Mount Mang, Xingqing rescued Gao Huan from peril and was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 神武歎曰：「富貴定在天也！」

translations.literal: Gao Huan sighed and said: "Wealth and honor are surely fixed in Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sighed and said, "Wealth and rank are fixed in Heaven!

sentences.zh: 猛竟如相者言，卒以榮寵自畢。

translations.literal: Meng in the end was just as the physiognomist had said and finally completed his life in glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Meng proved the physiognomist right and lived out his days in glory and favor.

sentences.zh: 興慶事見《齊本紀》。

translations.literal: Xingqing's affair is seen in the Basic Annals of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqing's story appears in the Basic Annals of Qi.

sentences.zh: 興慶每入陣，常自署名於背。

translations.literal: Whenever Xingqing entered battle he always signed his own name on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xingqing went into battle he signed his own name on his back.

sentences.zh: 神武使求其屍，祭之。

translations.literal: Gao Huan had his corpse sought out and sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had his body recovered and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 於死處立浮圖，世謂高王浮圖云。

translations.literal: At the place of his death a stupa was erected; the age calls it the Prince Gao Stupa.
translations.idiomatic: A stupa was raised where he fell; later ages called it the Prince Gao Stupa.

sentences.zh: 於是超贈儀同、涇州刺史，諡曰閔壯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Parallels and made governor of Jing, with posthumous name Minzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posthumously made grand master of splendid parallels and governor of Jing, with the posthumous name Minzhuang.

sentences.zh: 元景安

translations.literal: Yuan Jingan
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jingan

sentences.zh: 元景安，河南洛陽人，魏昭成皇帝之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Jingan was a man of Luoyang in Henan, a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jingan came from Luoyang in Henan and was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖虔，陳留王。

translations.literal: His ancestor Qian was Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Qian was Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 景安沈敏有幹局，少工騎射，善於事人。

translations.literal: Jingan was deep, keen, and capable; from youth he was skilled at mounted archery and good at serving men.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan was deep, keen, and capable; from youth he excelled at mounted archery and knew how to win men.

sentences.zh: 父永啟回代郡公授之。

translations.literal: His father Yong memorialized to transfer back the Duke of Dai commandery and bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong memorialized to transfer the Duke of Dai commandery back to him.

sentences.zh: 隨魏孝武帝西入關。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west through the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 天平末，周、齊交戰，景安臨陣東歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping Zhou and Qi fought each other; Jingan on the field returned east.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianping, as Zhou and Qi fought, Jingan surrendered on the field and returned east.

sentences.zh: 芒山之戰，以功賜爵西華縣男，代郡公如故。

translations.literal: In the battle at Mount Mang, for merit he was given the title Baron of Xihua county; the Duke of Dai commandery remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang he was rewarded with Baron of Xihua county for his merit; the Duke of Dai commandery remained as before.

sentences.zh: 景安妙閑馳騁，有容則，每梁使至，恆與斛律光、皮景和等對客騎射，見者稱善。

translations.literal: Jingan was skilled and practiced at galloping and riding, with bearing and measure; whenever Liang envoys came he was always with Hulu Guang, Pi Jinghe, and others to receive the guests in mounted archery, and onlookers praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan was skilled at the gallop and had dignified bearing; whenever Liang envoys arrived he was always ordered with Hulu Guang, Pi Jinghe, and others to receive them in mounted archery, and onlookers praised the display.

sentences.zh: 天保初，別封興勢伯，帶定襄縣令，賜姓高氏，累遷兼七兵尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao he was separately enfeoffed Earl of Xingshi, held the magistracy of Dingxiang, was granted the surname Gao, and was repeatedly promoted to concurrent minister of the seven armories.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was separately enfeoffed Earl of Xingshi, made magistrate of Dingxiang, granted the surname Gao, and rose to concurrent minister of the seven armories.

sentences.zh: 時初築長城，鎮戍未立，詔景安與諸將緣塞以備守。

translations.literal: At that time the long wall was first being built and frontier garrisons were not yet established; an edict ordered Jingan with the various generals to patrol the frontier for defense.
translations.idiomatic: The long wall was then first being built and frontier garrisons were not yet in place; an edict ordered Jingan and the other generals to patrol the frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 督領既多，且所部軍人富於財物，遂賄貨公行。

translations.literal: Because the command was broad and the troops under him were rich in goods, bribery soon ran openly.
translations.idiomatic: The command was broad and his troops were wealthy; bribery soon flourished openly.

sentences.zh: 文宣聞之，遣使推檢，唯景安纖毫無犯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan heard of it and sent envoys to investigate; only Jingan had not the slightest offense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan heard of it and sent investigators; only Jingan was without the slightest taint.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉歎，乃以所斂贓絹五百匹賜，以彰清節。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and sighed over it, then bestowed on him five hundred bolts of confiscated graft silk to display pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him deeply and bestowed five hundred bolts of the confiscated graft silk on him to honor his integrity.

sentences.zh: 孝昭嘗與功臣西園宴射，侯去堂一百三十步，中的者賜以良馬及金玉錦彩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao once held a banquet archery contest with meritorious ministers in the Western Garden; the target stood one hundred thirty paces from the hall, and whoever hit the mark was given fine horses and gold, jade, and brocade silks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao once held an archery feast with meritorious ministers in the Western Garden. The target stood one hundred thirty paces from the hall; whoever hit it received fine horses and gifts of gold, jade, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 有一人射中獸頭，去鼻寸餘。

translations.literal: One man shot the beast's head, a little more than an inch from the nose.
translations.idiomatic: One man struck the beast's head, missing the nose by little more than an inch.

sentences.zh: 唯景安最後，有矢未發。

translations.literal: Only Jingan was last, with an arrow not yet loosed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan shot last, with one arrow still unspent.

sentences.zh: 帝令景安解之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jingan to draw and release it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Jingan to take his shot.

sentences.zh: 景安引滿，正中獸鼻。

translations.literal: Jingan drew to the full and struck the beast's nose squarely.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan drew to the full and struck the beast's nose dead center.

sentences.zh: 帝嗟異稱善，特賞馬二匹，玉帛雜物，又加常等。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in wonder and praised it; he specially rewarded two horses, jade silks and miscellaneous goods, and added to the usual grade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and praised him, specially rewarding two horses, jade silks, and other gifts beyond the usual prize.

sentences.zh: 天統四年，除豫州刺史，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiantong he was made governor of Yu and given Opening Office, Grand Master of Splendid Parallels of Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tiantong he was made governor of Yu and given opening office with grand master of splendid parallels of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 武平三年，授行台尚書令，刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he was given circuit director of the masters of writing while his governorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he was made circuit director of the masters of writing while keeping the governorship.

sentences.zh: 封曆陽郡王。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Prince of Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Prince of Liyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 景安久在邊州，人物安之。

translations.literal: Jingan was long on the frontier; men and affairs were settled under him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan served long on the frontier, and the people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 又管內蠻多華少，景安被以恩威，咸得寧輯。

translations.literal: Moreover within his jurisdiction barbarians were many and Chinese few; Jingan covered them with kindness and awe, and all attained quiet order.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction barbarians were many and Chinese few; Jingan governed them with kindness and sternness until all were settled.

sentences.zh: 武平末，徵拜領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was summoned and appointed grand general of the palace garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was summoned and made grand general of the palace garrison.

sentences.zh: 入周，以大將軍、義甯郡公討稽胡，戰沒。

translations.literal: He entered Zhou; as grand general and Duke of Yining commandery he campaigned against the Ji Hu and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zhou; as grand general and Duke of Yining commandery he campaigned against the Ji Hu and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，永兄祚襲爵陳留王。

translations.literal: Earlier Yong's elder brother Zuo inherited the title Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yong's elder brother Zuo had inherited the title Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祚卒，子景皓嗣。

translations.literal: When Zuo died, his son Jinghao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo died, his son Jinghao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 天保時誅諸元親近者，如景安之徙疏宗，議請姓高氏。

translations.literal: In Tianbao, when the Yuan kin who were close associates were executed, such distant collateral clans as Jingan's branch were discussed for petition to take the surname Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao, when the Yuan who were close associates were executed, distant collateral lines such as Jingan's clan were ordered to take the surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 景皓云：「豈得棄本宗，遂他姓？

translations.literal: Jinghao said: "How can one abandon one's own clan and then take another surname?
translations.idiomatic: Jinghao said, "How can one abandon one's own clan and take another surname?

sentences.zh: 大丈夫寧可玉碎，不能瓦全。」

translations.literal: A great man would rather jade shatter than tiles be made whole.
translations.idiomatic: A true man would rather be jade shattered than tile made whole.

sentences.zh: 景安以白文宣，乃收景皓誅之，家屬徙彭城。

translations.literal: Jingan reported this to Emperor Wenxuan; Jinghao was then seized and executed, and his household was moved to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan reported this to Emperor Wenxuan. Jinghao was seized and executed, and his household was exiled to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 由是景安獨賜姓高氏，自外聽從本姓。

translations.literal: Because of this Jingan alone was granted the surname Gao; all others were permitted to keep their original surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter only Jingan was granted the surname Gao; all others were allowed to keep their original surnames.

sentences.zh: 永弟種子豫，字景豫，美容儀，有器幹。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Zhong's son Yu, courtesy name Jingyu, had fine looks and bearing and had capacity and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's younger brother Zhong's son Yu, courtesy name Jingyu, was handsome and capable.

sentences.zh: 景安告景皓慢言，引豫，雲相應和。

translations.literal: Jingan reported Jinghao's disrespectful words and implicated Yu, saying he had echoed them in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Jingan reported Jinghao's disrespectful words and implicated Yu, claiming he had echoed them.

sentences.zh: 豫占云：「爾時以衣袖掩景皓口，云：莫妄言。」

translations.literal: Yu, when questioned, said: "At that time I covered Jinghao's mouth with my sleeve and said: Do not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said under questioning, "At the time I covered Jinghao's mouth with my sleeve and told him not to speak rashly.

sentences.zh: 問景皓，與豫同，獲免。

translations.literal: When Jinghao was questioned he said the same as Yu, and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghao, questioned, said the same, and was spared.

sentences.zh: 卒于東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in office as governor of Eastern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as governor of Eastern Xu.

sentences.zh: 獨孤永業

translations.literal: Dugu Yongye
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yongye

sentences.zh: 獨孤永業，字世基。

translations.literal: Dugu Yongye, courtesy name Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yongye, courtesy name Shiji.

sentences.zh: 本姓劉，中山人也，母改適獨孤氏，永業幼隨母，為獨孤家養，遂從其姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was Liu; he was a man of Zhongshan. His mother remarried into the Dugu clan; Yongye in youth followed his mother and was raised in the Dugu household, and therefore took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally surnamed Liu and came from Zhongshan. His mother remarried into the Dugu clan; Yongye followed her in youth, was raised in their household, and took their surname.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao he was made secretariat vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was made secretariat vice-director.

sentences.zh: 永業解書計，善歌舞，甚為文宣所知。

translations.literal: Yongye understood writing and reckoning and excelled at song and dance; he was greatly known to Emperor Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye was literate and numerate, excelled at song and dance, and came to Emperor Wenxuan's notice.

sentences.zh: 後為洛州刺史、河陽行台左丞，甚有威信。

translations.literal: Later he was governor of Luo and left assistant commissioner of the Heyang Circuit, with great prestige and authority.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became governor of Luo and left assistant commissioner on the Heyang circuit, with great prestige.

sentences.zh: 遷行台尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to circuit senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to circuit senior minister.

sentences.zh: 永業久在河陽，善於招撫，周人憚之。

translations.literal: Yongye was long at Heyang and was skilled at winning over and pacifying; Zhou men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye had long served at Heyang and was skilled at winning people over; the Zhou learned to fear him.

sentences.zh: 姓鯁直，不交權勢。

translations.literal: By nature blunt and upright, he did not associate with men of power.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he kept no company with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 斛律光求二婢，弗得，毀之於朝廷。

translations.literal: Hulü Guang sought two maidservants and failed to obtain them; he slandered Yongye at court.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Guang asked for two maidservants and was refused; he slandered Yongye at court.

sentences.zh: 河清末，徵為太僕卿，以乞伏貴和代之，於是西境蹙弱，河洛人情騷動。

translations.literal: Late in Heqing he was summoned as grand minister of studs and replaced by Qifu Guihe; the western border then grew cramped and weak, and the mood in Heyang and Luoyang turned restless.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Heqing he was recalled as grand minister of studs and replaced by Qifu Guihe. The western frontier weakened at once, and Heyang and Luoyang grew restless.

sentences.zh: 武平三年，遣永業取斛律豐洛，因以為北道行台僕射、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping he was sent to take Hulü Fengluo and was made right vice minister of the Northern Circuit and governor of You.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuping he was sent to take Hulü Fengluo and was made right vice minister of the northern circuit and governor of You.

sentences.zh: 河洛人庶多思永業，又除河陽道行台、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: The people of Heyang and Luoyang mostly missed Yongye; he was again made right vice minister of the Heyang Circuit and governor of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Heyang and Luoyang missed him; he was again made right vice minister of the Heyang circuit and governor of Luo.

sentences.zh: 周武帝親攻金墉，永業出兵禦之，問是何達官，作何行動。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou personally attacked Jinyong; Yongye led troops to meet him and asked what eminent official this was and what he was doing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou attacked Jinyong in person. Yongye marched out to meet him and called, "What great man is that, and what is he up to?"

sentences.zh: 周人曰：「至尊自來，主人何不出看客？」

translations.literal: The Zhou men said: "His Majesty has come himself—why does our host not come out to receive the guest?
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou answered, "His Majesty has come in person. Why does our host not come out to greet his guest?

sentences.zh: 永業曰：「客行匆匆，故不出看。」

translations.literal: Yongye said: "The guest travels in haste—that is why I do not come out to look."
translations.idiomatic: Yongye said, "The guest is in too great a hurry—that is why I do not come out."

sentences.zh: 乃通夜辦馬槽二千。

translations.literal: He then spent the whole night preparing two thousand horse troughs.
translations.idiomatic: That night he had two thousand horse troughs prepared.

sentences.zh: 周人聞之，以為大軍至，乃去。

translations.literal: The Zhou men heard of it, thought a great army had arrived, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou heard of it, thought a great army had arrived, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進位開府、臨川王。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Opening Office and Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to opening office and Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 有甲士三萬。

translations.literal: He had thirty thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded thirty thousand armored troops.

sentences.zh: 聞晉州敗，請出兵北討，奏寢不報，永業慨憤。

translations.literal: When he heard of Jinzhou's defeat he requested to lead troops north to campaign; his memorials slept without reply, and Yongye sighed in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Jinzhou had fallen he asked to march north to fight; his memorials went unanswered, and Yongye burned with indignation.

sentences.zh: 又聞并州亦陷，乃遣子須達告降于周。

translations.literal: When he also heard that Bingzhou had fallen he sent his son Xuda to announce surrender to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When he also heard Bingzhou had fallen he sent his son Xuda to offer surrender to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 授上柱國、應公。

translations.literal: He was given Upper Pillar of State and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was made upper pillar of state and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 宣政末，為襄州總管。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanzheng he was made commander-in-chief of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanzheng he was made commander-in-chief of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，為行軍總管崔彥睦所殺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was killed by campaign commander-in-chief Cui Yanmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang he was killed by campaign commander-in-chief Cui Yanmu.

sentences.zh: 鮮于世榮

translations.literal: Xianyu Shirong
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Shirong

sentences.zh: 鮮于世榮，漁陽人也。

translations.literal: Xianyu Shirong was a man of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Shirong came from Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 父寶業，懷朔鎮將。

translations.literal: His father Baoye was garrison commander of Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baoye was garrison commander of Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 武平初，贈儀同三司、祠部尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Wuping he was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Parallels of Third Rank and minister of the ancestral shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuping he was posthumously made grand master of splendid parallels of the third rank and minister of the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 世榮少沈敏，有器幹。

translations.literal: Shirong in youth was deep and keen and had capacity and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong in youth was deep, keen, and capable.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，為神武親信都督，稍遷平西將軍，賜爵石門縣子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was trusted attendant commander for Gao Huan; he was gradually promoted to general who pacifies the west and given the title Viscount of Shimen county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe he became Gao Huan's trusted attendant commander, was gradually promoted to general who pacifies the west, and was enfeoffed Viscount of Shimen county.

sentences.zh: 天統二年，累加開府儀同三司，除鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiantong he was repeatedly given Opening Office, Grand Master of Splendid Parallels of Third Rank, and made governor of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiantong he received opening office with grand master of splendid parallels of the third rank and was made governor of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 武平中，以領軍從平高思好，封義陽郡王、領軍大將軍、太子太傅。

translations.literal: In Wuping, as director of the guard corps he followed in the pacification of Gao Sihao and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang commandery, grand general of the palace garrison, and grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping, as director of the guard corps he followed the pacification of Gao Sihao and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang commandery, made grand general of the palace garrison and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 及周武帝入代，送馬腦酒鐘與之，得便撞破。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou entered Dai he sent him agate wine goblets; Shirong took the chance and smashed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou entered Dai he sent agate wine goblets; Shirong seized the chance and smashed them.

sentences.zh: 周兵入鄴，諸將皆降，世榮在三台之前，獨鳴鼓不輟。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops entered Ye all the generals surrendered; Shirong before the Three Platforms alone beat the drum without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops entered Ye the generals all surrendered; Shirong alone before the Three Platforms kept beating the drum without cease.

sentences.zh: 及被執不屈，乃見殺。

translations.literal: When he was seized he would not yield and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Seized, he would not yield and was killed.

sentences.zh: 世榮雖武人，無文藝，以朝危政亂，每常竊歎。

translations.literal: Although Shirong was a military man without literary arts, because the court was perilous and government chaotic he often sighed to himself in private.
translations.idiomatic: Though a soldier without literary polish, he often sighed in private at the court's peril and the chaos of government.

sentences.zh: 見徵稅無厭，賞賜過度，發言歎息焉。

translations.literal: Seeing levies without end and rewards beyond measure, he spoke out in sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing taxes levied without end and rewards lavished beyond measure, he spoke out in sighs.

sentences.zh: 子貞，武平末，假儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Zhen, at the end of Wuping, was given acting Grand Master of Splendid Parallels of Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen, at the end of Wuping, was given acting grand master of splendid parallels of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 傅伏，太安人也。

translations.literal: Fu Fu was a man of Tai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Fu came from Tai'an.

sentences.zh: 少從戎，以戰功。

translations.literal: In youth he followed the army and rose through battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took the army young and rose through battle merit.

sentences.zh: 稍至開府、永橋領人大都督。

translations.literal: He gradually reached Opening Office and grand commander of the Yong Bridge tribal settlement.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually rose to opening office and grand commander of the Yong Bridge tribal settlement.

sentences.zh: 周武帝前攻河陰，伏自永橋夜入中氵單城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou earlier attacked Heyin, Fu from Yong Bridge by night entered Zhongtan fortress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou advanced on Heyin, Fu crossed from Yong Bridge at night and entered Zhongtan fortress.

sentences.zh: 南城陷，被圍二旬不下。

translations.literal: The south city fell; he was besieged for twenty days and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The south city fell, yet he held under siege for twenty days without yielding.

sentences.zh: 救兵至，周師還。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived the Zhou army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Relief came and the Zhou withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後除東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made governor of Eastern Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Eastern Yong.

sentences.zh: 周克晉州，執行台尉相貴。

translations.literal: When Zhou took Jinzhou they seized circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou took Jinzhou they seized circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui.

sentences.zh: 招伏，伏不從。

translations.literal: They summoned Fu to surrender; Fu would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Fu to surrender; he refused.

sentences.zh: 周克并州，遺韋孝寬以伏子世寬來招伏，授上大將軍、武鄉郡公，即給告身，以金馬腦二酒鐘為信。

translations.literal: When Zhou took Bingzhou they sent Wei Xiaokuan with Fu's son Shikuan to summon Fu; he was given Grand General and Duke of Wuxiang commandery, and at once credentials were issued, with two golden agate wine goblets as pledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou took Bingzhou they sent Wei Xiaokuan with Fu's son Shikuan to win him over, appointing him grand general and Duke of Wuxiang commandery, issuing his commission at once, with two golden agate wine goblets as pledge.

sentences.zh: 伏不受曰：「事君，有死無二。

translations.literal: Fu would not accept and said: "In serving one's lord there is death but no second loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused and said, "To serve one's lord is to die without a second loyalty.

sentences.zh: 此兒為臣不能竭忠，為子不能盡孝，人所仇疾，願即斬之，以號令天下。」

translations.literal: This son as minister cannot exhaust loyalty, as son cannot exhaust filial piety—what men hate and detest—I wish immediately to behead him, to command all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: This boy has failed as a minister to give his lord full loyalty and as a son to show full filial devotion—men despise him. I beg that he be executed at once, as a warning to all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 周武自鄴還至晉州，遣高阿那肱等臨汾召伏。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou from Ye returned to Jinzhou, sent Gao Anagub and others to Fen to summon Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou returned from Ye to Jinzhou and sent Gao Anagub and others to Fen to summon Fu.

sentences.zh: 伏聞後主已被獲，仰天大哭，率眾入城，於査事前，北面哭良久，然後降。

translations.literal: Fu heard the Later Ruler had already been captured, looked up to Heaven and wept greatly, led the multitude into the city, before the inquiry office faced north and wept long, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu heard the Later Ruler had been taken, he looked up to Heaven and wailed. He led his troops into the city, knelt facing north before the inquiry office, and wept a long while before he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 周武見曰：「何不早降？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou met him and said: "Why not surrender early?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu received him and said, "Why did you not surrender sooner?"

sentences.zh: 伏流涕曰：「臣三世衣食齊家，被任如此，革命不能自死，羞見天地。」

translations.literal: Fu shed tears and said: "Your servant three generations fed on Qi, was entrusted thus—at the dynastic turn could not die by his own hand, ashamed to face Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Fu wept and said, "Three generations of my house have lived on Qi's bounty. Entrusted as I was, when the dynasty fell I could not die by my own hand—I am ashamed to face Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 周武親執手曰：「為臣當若此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu personally took his hand and said: "As minister one should be like this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand and said, "This is how a minister ought to be.

sentences.zh: 朕平齊，唯見公一人。」

translations.literal: In pacifying Qi I have seen only you, sir, alone."
translations.idiomatic: In pacifying Qi I have found only you, sir."

sentences.zh: 乃自食一羊肋，以骨賜伏，曰：「骨親肉疏，所以相付。」

translations.literal: He then himself ate one lamb rib, with the bone gifted Fu, saying: "Bone is close, flesh is distant—therefore I entrust this to you."
translations.idiomatic: He ate a lamb rib himself, then gave Fu the bone, saying, "The bone is kin; the flesh is apart—therefore I entrust this to you."

sentences.zh: 遂引與同食。

translations.literal: He then drew him to eat together.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him sit and eat with him.

sentences.zh: 令于侍伯色宿衛，授上儀同，敕之曰：「若即與公高官，恐歸投者心動。

translations.literal: He ordered Yu Shibose to guard on night duty, granted Senior Pillar of State, charged him saying: "If at once I give you, sir, high office, I fear those who come over will waver in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yu Shibose on night guard over him and made him Senior Pillar of State, telling him, "If I raise you to high rank at once, those who have just defected may grow restless.

sentences.zh: 勿慮不富貴。」

translations.literal: Do not worry that you will not be rich and honored."
translations.idiomatic: Do not fear that you will lack wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 又問：「前救河陰得何官？」

translations.literal: He also asked: "When you earlier saved Heyin, what office did you receive?"
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "When you held Heyin, what rank did you receive?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「蒙一轉，授特進、永昌郡公。」

translations.literal: He said: "I received one promotion, was made Superlative Pillar and Duke of Yongchang commandery."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I was promoted once—to Superlative Pillar and Duke of Yongchang commandery."

sentences.zh: 周武謂後主曰：「朕前三年，決意取河陰，正為傅伏不可動。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou said to the Later Ruler: "Three years ago I resolved to take Heyin—it was precisely because Fu Fu could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said to the Later Ruler, "Three years ago I set my mind on taking Heyin—and it was solely because Fu Fu could not be budged.

sentences.zh: 公當時賞授，何其薄也？」

translations.literal: Your reward and appointment at the time—how meager!"
translations.idiomatic: The reward you gave him then—how paltry!"

sentences.zh: 賜伏金酒卮。

translations.literal: He gifted Fu a golden wine goblet.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Fu a golden wine cup.

sentences.zh: 後以為岷州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made governor of Minzhou and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed governor of Minzhou and soon died.

sentences.zh: 齊軍晉州敗後，兵將罕有全節。

translations.literal: After the Qi army's defeat at Jinzhou, officers and men rarely kept integrity whole.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi army's rout at Jinzhou, few officers and men kept their honor intact.

sentences.zh: 有其殺身成仁者，有儀同叱于苟生。

translations.literal: Some there were who achieved death for fulfillment of humanity—such as Pillar-of-State Chiyu Gusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Some died to fulfill humanity's highest call—among them Pillar-of-State Chiyu Gusheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮南兗州。

translations.literal: He guarded southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周武破鄴，赦書至，苟生自縊死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou took Ye, the amnesty arrived; Gusheng hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gusheng hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 又有開府、中侍中、宦者田敬宣，本字鵬，蠻人也。

translations.literal: There was also Opening Office, Palace Attendant within the Seraglio, eunuch Tian Jingxuan—original courtesy name Peng, a Man tribesman.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Opening Office and Palace Attendant within the Seraglio, the eunuch Tian Jingxuan—courtesy name Peng—a Man tribesman.

sentences.zh: 年十四五，便好讀書。

translations.literal: At fourteen or fifteen he already loved reading books.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen or fifteen he was already devoted to books.

sentences.zh: 既為閽寺，伺隙便周章詢請。

translations.literal: Once he was in the gate-guard service, whenever he found a gap he would bustle about with inquiries and requests.
translations.idiomatic: Once he served in the gate-guard, he seized every opening to hurry about with questions and pleas.

sentences.zh: 每至文林館，氣喘汗流，問書之外，不暇他語。

translations.literal: Whenever he reached the Forest of Letters Hall, panting and streaming sweat—beyond asking about books he had no leisure for other talk.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reached the Forest of Letters Hall he came panting, sweat streaming down—beyond questions of books he had breath for nothing else.

sentences.zh: 及視古人節義事，未嘗不感激沈吟。

translations.literal: When he viewed ancient men's integrity and righteousness, never did he fail to be moved to sigh and murmur.
translations.idiomatic: When he read of ancient men's integrity and righteousness, he was always stirred to sigh and murmur long.

sentences.zh: 顏之推重其勤學，甚加開獎。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui valued his diligent study and greatly encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui prized his zeal for learning and encouraged him warmly.

sentences.zh: 後遂通顯。

translations.literal: Later he rose to full prominence.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 後主之奔青州，遣其西出參伺動靜，為周軍所獲。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler fled to Qingzhou, he sent him west to reconnoiter movements; he was seized by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler fled to Qingzhou, he sent Jingxuan west to watch the enemy's movements; Zhou troops captured him.

sentences.zh: 問齊主何在，紿雲已去。

translations.literal: Asked where the Qi lord was, he deceived them saying he had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where the Qi ruler was, he lied that he had already fled.

sentences.zh: 毆捶服之。

translations.literal: Beaten until they believed it.
translations.idiomatic: They beat him until he yielded the truth.

sentences.zh: 每折一肢，辭色愈厲，竟斷四體而卒。

translations.literal: Each time a limb was broken his expression grew fiercer; in the end when all four limbs were broken he died.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a limb was broken his bearing grew fiercer; when all four were severed at last, he died.

sentences.zh: 又有雷顯和，晉州敗後，為建州道行台左僕射。

translations.literal: There was also Lei Xianhe; after the Jinzhou defeat he was Left Vice President of the Jianzhou Circuit Platform.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lei Xianhe, who after the Jinzhou defeat became Left Vice President of the Jianzhou Circuit Platform.

sentences.zh: 周武帝使其子招焉，顯和禁其子而不受。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou sent his son to summon him; Xianhe restrained his son and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou sent his son to win him over; Xianhe kept his son from going and refused.

sentences.zh: 聞鄴城敗，乃降。

translations.literal: When he heard Ye had fallen, then he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Ye had fallen, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 後主失并州，使開府紇奚永安告急於突厥他缽略可汗。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler lost Bingzhou, he sent Opening Office Hexi Yong'an to urge emergency aid on the Türk Tabo Lüe Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler lost Bingzhou, he sent Opening Office Hexi Yong'an to beg urgent aid of the Türk Qaghan Tabo Lüe.

sentences.zh: 及聞齊滅，他缽處永安於吐谷渾使下。

translations.literal: When they heard Qi had perished, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Qi had fallen, Tabo placed Yong'an under a Tuyuhun envoy.

sentences.zh: 永安抗言曰：「本國既敗，永安豈惜賤命？

translations.literal: Yong'an spoke defiantly: "My state is already defeated—would Yong'an spare his base life?
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an spoke defiantly: "My state is already lost—why should Yong'an cling to this worthless life?

sentences.zh: 欲閉氣自絕，恐天下不知大齊有死節臣。

translations.literal: I wished to hold my breath and end myself, but feared men under Heaven would not know Great Qi had a minister who died for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to hold my breath and die, but feared the world would never know that Great Qi had a minister who died for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 唯乞一刀，以顯示遠近。」

translations.literal: I ask only for one blade, to show it to near and far."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only for a blade, that near and far may see it."

sentences.zh: 他缽嘉之，贈馬七十疋，歸之。

translations.literal: Tabo commended him, gifted seventy horses, and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo praised him, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 又有代人高寶甯，武平末，為營州刺史，鎮黃龍。

translations.literal: There was also Dai man Gao Baoning; at the end of the Wuping era he was governor of Yingzhou, garrisoning Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Dai man Gao Baoning, who at the end of the Wuping era was governor of Yingzhou, holding Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 夷夏重其威信。

translations.literal: Barbarians and Chinese alike respected his prestige and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians and Chinese alike honored his authority and good faith.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，遺信招慰，不受敕書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi he sent envoys with letters of reassurance; he would not accept the imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi he sent envoys to reassure him; Baoning would not accept the imperial writ.

sentences.zh: 范陽王紹義在突厥中，寶寧上表勸進。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was among the Türks; Baoning submitted a memorial urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fanyang Shaoyi was with the Türks; Baoning memorialized urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 范陽王署寶甯為丞相。

translations.literal: Prince of Fanyang appointed Baoning Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fanyang named Baoning his Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及盧昌期據范陽起兵，寶寧引紹義集夷夏兵數萬救之。

translations.literal: When Lu Changqi held Fanyang and raised troops, Baoning led Shaoyi to gather barbarian and Chinese troops numbering tens of thousands to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Changqi seized Fanyang and raised arms, Baoning brought Shaoyi to gather tens of thousands of barbarian and Chinese troops to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 至潞河，知周將宇文神舉屠范陽，還據黃龍。

translations.literal: Reaching Lu River, learning Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had slaughtered Fanyang, he withdrew to hold Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: At the Lu River he learned that the Zhou general Yuwen Shenju had sacked Fanyang; he turned back to hold Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 論曰：爾硃殘逆，遠效誠款，知神武陵逼，隨帝西遷，去就之途，未為失節。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: When Erzhu was cruel and perverse, [some] from afar offered sincere allegiance; knowing Shenju of Shen's pressing threat, they followed the emperor west—on the path of coming and going they did not lose integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: When the Erzhu clan turned cruel and perverse, some from afar still offered sincere allegiance. Seeing Yuwen Shenju's pressing threat, they followed the emperor west; on the road of departure and return they did not lose their integrity.

sentences.zh: 道元感母兄之戀，荷知遇之恩，思親懷舊，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Daoyuan was moved by love for mother and elder brother, bore grace for knowing encounter—thinking of kin and old home was certainly fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan was moved by love for mother and elder brother and bore the debt of one who had been recognized and favored; to think of kin and old home was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 生不屈西朝，歸誠河朔；

translations.literal: Sheng would not bend to the Western court and turned sincerity to the north of the River;
translations.idiomatic: Sheng would not bow to the Western court and turned his loyalty to the north of the River;

sentences.zh: 保年之於開，義異策名。

translations.literal: Baonian's relation to Kai was righteousness unlike merely taking a name [in service];
translations.idiomatic: Baonian's stand toward Kai was a different kind of righteousness than merely enrolling one's name;

sentences.zh: 並乘幾獨運，異夫盜寶竊邑者也。

translations.literal: all seized the moment and acted alone—differing from those who stole treasure and usurped towns.
translations.idiomatic: all seized the moment and acted on their own—unlike men who merely stole treasure and seized towns.

sentences.zh: 神武招攜，理殊納叛；

translations.literal: When Shenwu recruited and comforted, it was reason unlike receiving rebels;
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan drew men in and supported them, it was a different matter from merely taking in defectors;

sentences.zh: 諸將擇木，情非背恩，故能各立功名，終極榮寵。

translations.literal: The generals chose their tree—the feeling was not betrayal of grace; therefore each could stand merit and in the end reach glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The generals chose where to roost; their hearts were not turned from gratitude. Thus each could build his merit and in the end win glory and favor.

sentences.zh: 神敬力屈東維，未虧臣節，其被恩化，蓋亦明主之仁焉。

translations.literal: Shenjing's strength broke in the eastern regions; he did not harm ministerial integrity—his receiving grace and transformation was surely also the benevolence of a bright lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjing's strength failed in the eastern marches, yet he did not stain his minister's integrity; that he received grace and was transformed shows also the benevolence of a discerning lord.

sentences.zh: 劉貴、蔡俊有先見之明，匡贊霸業，配饗清廟，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: Liu Gui and Cai Jun had foresight, aided and praised the hegemonic enterprise—sharing sacrifice in the Pure Temple—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui and Cai Jun had foresight and helped raise the hegemonic enterprise; that they share sacrifice in the Pure Temple was surely not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 韓賢、尉長命、王懷、任祥、莫多婁貸文、厙狄回洛，厙狄盛、張保洛、侯莫陳相、薛孤延、斛律羌舉、張瓊、宋顯、王則等，並運屬時來。

translations.literal: Han Xian, Wei Zhangming, Wang Huai, Ren Xiang, Moduoluo Daiwen, Shedi Huiluo, Shedi Sheng, Zhang Baoluo, Houmo Chenxiang, Xue Guyan, Hulu Qiangju, Zhang Qiong, Song Xian, Wang Ze and others—all were borne when fortune came.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xian, Wei Zhangming, Wang Huai, Ren Xiang, Moduoluo Daiwen, Shedi Huiluo, Shedi Sheng, Zhang Baoluo, Houmo Chenxiang, Xue Guyan, Hulu Qiangju, Zhang Qiong, Song Xian, Wang Ze, and others—all rode the tide of their time.

sentences.zh: 或因ＩＵ旅，馮附末光，申其志力，化為王侯，固為宜矣。

translations.literal: Some through ＩＵ travel leaned on the last gleam, exerted their will and strength, and were transformed into kings and marquises—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Some, as men on the road, clung to the last gleam of fortune, gave their will and strength full play, and were raised to kings and marquises—which was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 孝卿功臣之胤，自致公卿，立履之地，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: Xiaoxing was scion of meritorious ministers, himself reaching duke and minister; standing and treading where he did is also enough to be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxing was heir to a house of merit and reached duke and minister by his own effort; the ground on which he stood is also worth praise.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗兵機武略，在世見重，昔事爾硃，固執忠義，不用范曾之言，終見烏江之禍。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong in military craft and martial strategy was valued in his age; once serving Erzhu he held fast to loyalty and righteousness; not using Fan Zeng's words, in the end met the calamity of Black River.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong's military craft and martial strategy were prized in his age. Once in Erzhu's service, he held fast to loyalty and righteousness; refusing counsel like Fan Zeng's, he met at last the disaster of the Black River.

sentences.zh: 侯景狼戾，固非後主之臣；

translations.literal: Hou Jing was ruthless and violent—certainly no minister of the Later Ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was savage and ungovernable—never truly a minister of the Later Ruler;

sentences.zh: 神武遺言，實表知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Shenwu's dying words truly show a mirror for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's dying words truly show how keenly he knew men.

sentences.zh: 寒山、渦水，往若摧枯，算盡數奇，逢斯禍酷，悲夫！

translations.literal: Hanshan and Guoshui—going forth like shattering dead wood; fate exhausted, numbers adverse—meeting such cruel disaster—alas!
translations.idiomatic: At Hanshan and the Guo River they swept forward like breaking dead wood—yet fate was spent and fortune turned strange, and they met so cruel a ruin. Alas!

sentences.zh: 三藏連屬危亡，貞概自處，可謂不隕門節矣。

translations.literal: Sanchang linked in crisis until ruin, upright integrity in his own conduct—it may be called not tarnishing his clan's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Sanchang stood through linked crises until ruin, holding himself with upright integrity—it may be said he did not dim his house's honor.

sentences.zh: 叱列平、步大汗薩、薛脩義、慕容儼、潘樂、彭樂、暴顯、皮景和、綦連猛、元景安等，策名戎幕，備開夷險，位高任重，咸遂本誠。

translations.literal: Chi Lieping, Buda Hansa, Xue Xiuyi, Murong Yan, Pan Le, Peng Le, Bao Xian, Pi Jinghe, Qi Lianmeng, Yuan Jing'an and others—all enrolled names on the military curtain, fully tested through barbarian hardship and danger, high rank and heavy burden, all fulfilled their original sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Lieping, Buda Hansa, Xue Xiuyi, Murong Yan, Pan Le, Peng Le, Bao Xian, Pi Jinghe, Qi Lianmeng, Yuan Jing'an, and others enrolled their names on the war council, were tried through every hardship of campaign, rose to high rank and heavy trust, and all fulfilled their first loyalty.

sentences.zh: 永業、世榮之徒，國危方見忠節，不然，則丹青簡冊，安所貴乎。

translations.literal: Yongye, Shirong and such men—in national danger then showed loyal integrity; otherwise, on the scarlet silk and bamboo registers, wherein would they be prized?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yongye and Shirong showed their loyal integrity only when the state was in peril; otherwise, on what ground would the annals in scarlet and ink hold them dear?
